# DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics (DATAPKT)

> Drone survey, mapping, GIS and design company based in Gurugram, Haryana, India, founded on 14 September 2020. We survey, map and design for infrastructure projects; we do not build them. Empanelled with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in three zones for monthly drone survey work. DIPP-recognised start-up. Legal name: DATAPKT Private Limited.

## Key facts
- Founded on 14 September 2020; DIPP-recognised start-up
- Empanelled with NHAI in three zones for monthly drone survey work
- More than 3 lakh km of highway data captured in six years for highway authorities and private contractors, and more than 70,000 km in FY 2026-27
- 20+ drone pilots; each team covers about 35 km of highway a day for survey imagery or about 50 km a day for videography
- In-house GIS team working in ArcGIS, QGIS and AutoCAD
- Thermal team includes a thermographer certified to ISO 9712 Level 2
- Power-sector clients include NTPC and Adani
- 60+ railway Engineering Scale Plans, yard plans and drainage plans submitted; 32 more yards in progress

## What we do
- Drone and DGPS topographic surveys for highways, roads and expressways
- Railway and metro surveys, including Engineering Scale Plans (ESP), yard plans and drainage plans
- Survey and design inputs for Detailed Project Reports (DPRs)
- Drone thermal (infrared) inspection of solar power plants and electrical assets
- Transmission line route surveys and substation site surveys
- Water resources surveys and bathymetry for canals, rivers and reservoirs
- Photogrammetry: orthomosaics, digital terrain and surface models, contours and volumes
- LiDAR survey and classified point clouds
- Landslide and slope stability investigation, seismic refraction survey and slope protection design
- GIS mapping and data processing; remote GIS processing offered to clients outside India (all projects so far in India)
- Aerial videography and monthly progress videos for projects

## Sectors
Highways and roads, railways and metro, power and solar, water resources, urban planning, mining, oil and gas, environment, agriculture, archaeology, public safety, manufacturing and wildlife.

## Where we work
Projects across India from our Gurugram office. Remote GIS data processing is offered to clients outside India; all projects so far have been in India.

- [Water resources](https://datapkt.com/water-resource.html): drone surveys of rivers, lakes, canals and irrigation systems; topographic maps, depth and volume data, water quality readings, flood zone maps and 3D models

## Services in depth
- [Drone survey cost in India](https://datapkt.com/drone-survey-cost.html): sites quoted per acre or hectare, corridors per km; the six factors that decide the price, and what to send for a quote
- [Free drone survey calculators](https://datapkt.com/tools/): hub page for the GSD calculator (before the flight) and the checkpoint RMSE calculator (after processing)
- [Free drone GSD calculator](https://datapkt.com/tools/gsd-calculator.html): ground sample distance, image footprint and the flight height for a target GSD, with camera presets
- [Free checkpoint RMSE calculator](https://datapkt.com/tools/rmse-calculator.html): paste surveyed and map coordinates or residuals to get RMSE in X, Y and Z, horizontal RMSE (RMSEr), mean error per axis and the largest residual
- [Transmission line and substation survey and design](https://datapkt.com/transmission-line-substation-design.html): alternate routes and feasibility report, drone maps on khasra maps for land acquisition, detailed route survey with tower spotting, substation GAD and SLD
- [Drone transmission line inspection services](https://datapkt.com/transmission-line-drone-inspection.html): inspection of energised lines; patrol vs detailed tower inspection; zoom visual, radiometric thermal and LiDAR; hotspot grading (ANSI/NETA bands, 40%+ load); span-wise clearance measured against the owner's thresholds; tower-wise defect register; 10 to 15 towers a day per crew
- [Landslide and slope stability investigation and protection design](https://datapkt.com/landslide-slope-stability.html): drone LiDAR, seismic refraction tomography and geological mapping (RMR, GSI, SMR) in one ground model; stability analysis, hazard zonation and slope protection design
- [Seismic refraction survey and tomography (SRT)](https://datapkt.com/seismic-refraction-survey.html): soil thickness, depth to rock and weak zones for slopes, roads, tunnels, dams and foundations, read with drone LiDAR

## Guides
- [How accurate is a drone survey? GSD, GCPs and RTK explained](https://datapkt.com/insights/drone-survey-accuracy-gsd-gcp-rtk.html): a few centimetres with RTK or PPK and ground control, proved with independent checkpoints
- [ESP full form in railways: what is an Engineering Scale Plan?](https://datapkt.com/insights/what-is-an-engineering-scale-plan.html): what an ESP drawing shows, the scales used, who prepares it and how a drone survey produces one
- [Solar plant drone thermography: what the report should include](https://datapkt.com/insights/solar-plant-drone-thermography-report.html): defect type, location, temperature difference and severity under IEC TS 62446-3
- [Drone topographic survey for solar power plants: what developers need before design](https://datapkt.com/insights/solar-plant-topographic-survey.html): DTM, contours, obstructions and existing drainage; DGPS ground control and checkpoints; photogrammetry or LiDAR; catchments and flow paths from the DTM; deliverables in DWG, SHP, GeoTIFF and LAS
- [LiDAR vs photogrammetry: which drone survey to choose](https://datapkt.com/insights/lidar-vs-photogrammetry.html): accuracy on open ground and under vegetation, cost and deliverables, and which to choose by project type
- [Drone vs manual solar panel inspection: which finds more, faster?](https://datapkt.com/insights/drone-vs-manual-solar-panel-inspection.html): coverage, speed, what each finds and misses, IEC TS 62446-3 conditions and the drone-first workflow
- [Highway drone videography for NHAI projects: what the monthly video must show](https://datapkt.com/insights/nhai-highway-drone-videography.html): NHAI's monthly drone video rule, who flies, what each frame must show and Data Lake uploads
- [Transmission line drone inspection vs foot patrol: what each one catches](https://datapkt.com/insights/transmission-line-drone-inspection.html): drone, foot patrol or helicopter; thermal hotspot severity and tree clearance by voltage
- [Railway drone inspection: track, OHE, bridges and yards](https://datapkt.com/insights/railway-drone-inspection.html): OHE thermal checks, track surroundings, bridges under RDSO BS-129, yards and ESPs
- [Railway final location survey (FLS) by drone and LiDAR: what it covers](https://datapkt.com/insights/railway-final-location-survey.html): where the FLS sits after reconnaissance and PETS, the Engineering Code plans, sections and scales, and how drone and LiDAR survey with DGPS control fit
- [Topographic and contour survey by drone: method, accuracy and deliverables](https://datapkt.com/insights/topographic-survey-by-drone.html): when a drone fits, ground control and datum, choosing the contour interval from vertical RMSE, and DTM, contour, orthomosaic and point cloud deliverables
- [Bridge inspection by drone in India: what it can and cannot replace](https://datapkt.com/insights/bridge-inspection-by-drone.html): IRC:SP:35, IBMS, IRBM schedules and RDSO BS-129; what a drone does well, what still needs hands-on testing and an engineer, deliverables and a client checklist
- [Drone survey vs DGPS and total station: which should you use?](https://datapkt.com/insights/drone-survey-vs-dgps-total-station.html): what each method does best and why most infrastructure surveys combine all three
- [Drone survey permissions in India: Digital Sky, airspace zones and what a client should check](https://datapkt.com/insights/drone-survey-permissions-india.html): UIN, Remote Pilot Certificate, green, yellow and red zones (5, 8 and 12 km from airport perimeters), insurance and the 2021 geospatial guidelines
- [How to choose a drone survey company in India: a 10-point checklist](https://datapkt.com/insights/how-to-choose-a-drone-survey-company.html): certified pilots, accuracy reports, sample deliverables, references and data ownership
- [Drone survey deliverables explained: orthomosaic, DSM, DTM, contours and point clouds](https://datapkt.com/insights/drone-survey-deliverables-explained.html): what each deliverable is for and its file formats (GeoTIFF, LAS, DWG, SHP, KMZ)
- [Drone survey and geomatics glossary](https://datapkt.com/insights/drone-survey-glossary.html): plain-English definitions of GSD, GCP, RTK, DTM vs DSM, RMSE, LAS files, IEC TS 62446-3, PLS-CADD, ESP, OHE and seismic refraction
- [Drone survey for highway DPRs: what consultants need (IRC:SP:19)](https://datapkt.com/insights/drone-survey-for-highway-dpr.html): strip plan, contours, cross-sections and benchmarks; what a drone does well and what still needs ground survey
- [Landslide survey in India: methods, standards and what it costs](https://datapkt.com/insights/landslide-survey-india.html): drone LiDAR, seismic refraction, geological mapping, stability analysis, IS codes and what decides the cost
- [Point cloud classification explained: LAS classes, ground filtering and QC](https://datapkt.com/insights/point-cloud-classification.html): ASPRS LAS 1.4 class codes, ground filtering methods and failure modes, QC checks, deliverables and what to specify when outsourcing

About DATA PKT
# We survey, map and design the ground India builds on.
DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics is a drone survey, mapping, GIS and design company based in Gurugram, Haryana. Since 2020 our pilots, surveyors, GIS analysts and engineers have worked on highways, railways, solar plants, power lines, canals and mines across India.
## Company facts
Founded
14 September 2020
Recognition
DIPP-recognised start-up
NHAI
Empanelled in three zones for monthly drone survey work
Team
20+ pilots and an in-house GIS team
Thermography
Thermographer certified to ISO 9712 Level 2
Power-sector clients
Including NTPC and Adani
Office
434, 4th Floor, JMD Megapolis, Sohna Road, Sector 48, Gurugram 122018
Former name
Formerly known as DATA PKT Aviation
## What we do
We collect accurate data about the ground and the assets on it, and turn it into drawings, GIS layers and reports that engineers and owners can use. We survey, map and design for infrastructure projects; we do not construct them.
- Drone and DGPS topographic surveys for highways, roads, railways, canals and industrial sites
- Engineering Scale Plans , yard plans and DPR survey inputs for railway and road projects
- LiDAR surveys and classified point clouds, including terrain under vegetation
- Photogrammetry: orthomosaics, terrain and surface models, contours and volumes
- Drone thermal inspection of solar PV plants and electrical assets
- Transmission line route surveys and substation site surveys
- Water resources surveys and bathymetry for canals, rivers and reservoirs
- GIS mapping and data processing , with remote processing offered to clients outside India (all our projects so far have been in India)
- Aerial videography and monthly progress videos for projects
## How a project runs
- Scope: we agree the area or corridor, the accuracy needed, the coordinate system and the deliverables.
- Plan: flight plans, ground control layout and the permissions the site needs under India's drone rules.
- Capture: our pilots fly the site while surveyors measure ground control with DGPS.
- Process: the GIS team builds the orthomosaic, terrain models and point clouds and checks accuracy against independent checkpoints.
- Deliver: drawings, GIS layers and reports in the formats your team uses, with an accuracy report.
## Sectors
Highways and roads , railways and metro , power and solar , water resources , urban planning , mining , oil and gas , environment , agriculture and archaeology .

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What does DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics do?
We collect accurate data about the ground and the assets on it, and turn it into drawings, GIS layers and reports. Our work covers drone and DGPS topographic surveys, LiDAR, photogrammetry, thermal inspection of solar plants, transmission line and substation surveys, bathymetry, GIS processing and aerial videography. We survey, map and design; we do not construct.
Q: Where is DATA PKT based and where do you work?
Our office is at 434, 4th Floor, JMD Megapolis, Sohna Road, Sector 48, Gurugram, Haryana. We work on projects across India through our own pilots and a wider drone pilot network, and we also offer GIS mapping and remote data processing to clients outside India. All our projects so far have been in India.
Q: How much experience does DATA PKT have?
DATA PKT was founded on 14 September 2020 and is a DIPP-recognised start-up. In six years we have captured over 3 lakh km of highway data for authorities and private contractors. We have 20+ pilots and an in-house GIS team, and our work spans highways, railways, solar plants, power lines, canals and mines.
Q: How does a DATA PKT survey project run?
We agree the area, accuracy, coordinate system and deliverables; plan flights, ground control and the permissions needed under India's drone rules; fly the site while surveyors measure ground control with DGPS; process the orthomosaic, terrain models and point clouds and check them against independent checkpoints; then deliver drawings, GIS layers and reports with an accuracy report.

# We Automate with Drones
Flying for you. A detailed bird's eye view of your assets.
Get In Touch
## Why DATAPKT?
In a short span of time, DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics, a DIPP-recognized start-up, has captured 3 lakh+ km of highway data in six years for authorities and private contractors across India. We employ cutting-edge high-end technology like artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computer vision, which aids in the creation of business insights and the subsequent making of crucial business decisions. Only the work ethic of our team, who are committed to constant innovation and going above and beyond for our clients, could have made this all possible.
Data Acquisition
DATA PKT drones are the most effective visual asset, collecting consistent data into meaningful insights using machine learning algorithms. our drones capture object data in the crispest and most precise way possible, resulting in consistent data from the same angle and height as learned by its deep learning algorithms.
Data Processing
With the help of its aerial data processing solutions, DATA PKT gathers photogrammetric data of the highest possible quality, which is then precisely, swiftly, and affordably processed to produce ortho-rectified photos, 3D models, Digital terrain models, digital surface models, geotagging, and many more products. Utilizing its integrated source code systems, the data collected by OUR drone is analysed and turned into one-of-a-kind solutions for our clients.
Enabling AI Services
Real-time data and analytics are retrieved by utilising AI-driven software to automate operations. # Drone Survey for Highways and Roads
Drones record the condition of a road network at every stage of construction. Aerial surveys also cut down the number of site visits needed to record conditions and issues.
DATA PKT covers highway projects with drone, DGPS and LiDAR survey, from DPR survey through monthly construction monitoring to operation and maintenance.
In short: NHAI has made monthly drone video recording mandatory for national highway projects through construction, operation and maintenance, with comparative videos of the current and previous month uploaded to its Data Lake portal ( report ). DATA PKT is empanelled with NHAI in three zones for this monthly drone survey work and prepares the video project reports.
Pre-Construction
Under Construction
O & M
## Pre-Construction
Before construction the job is to get the ground right: a survey accurate enough to design on, a clear view of each candidate alignment, and quantities you can price.
Detailed Project Report (DPR)
### Surveying and Mapping
We fly the corridor with photogrammetry or LiDAR, tied to DGPS ground control points, and deliver an orthomosaic, terrain model, contours and existing features in CAD as the base for the DPR. Areas under dense tree cover, structures and cross-drainage details are completed with DGPS or total station.
### Site Inspection
Repeat flights give a dated, geo-referenced record of the site: what has been built, where the hazards are and whether work follows the drawings, shared with the authority and the contractor.
### Earthwork Monitoring
From each survey we compute stockpile volumes and cut and fill quantities, so earthwork can be measured, billed and checked against the schedule.
### Best Route Analysis
For a new alignment we map each proposed route, produce an orthomosaic, elevation model and contours, and check conflicts with existing and proposed structures. Revenue maps are digitised so land cost can be estimated alongside construction quantities, giving a like-for-like comparison of the routes.
## Under Construction
After the preparation of a detailed project report that sets out the Highway construction companies on a planned project path, DATAPKT provides the following services during the construction stage of the project:
### Progress Monitoring
Each flight is processed into a geometrically corrected orthophoto. Comparing orthophotos from different dates shows what has changed, the percentage of work completed and the likely completion date.
### Video Project Report ( VPR )
We fly the stretch once a month and produce a video project report with completion figures for each activity and site observations. Month-on-month comparison also flags new encroachments and buildings along the corridor.
### Utility Shifting
We map the stretches where utility lines are being shifted, track progress against the programme, flag clashes and safety risks, and report status so construction teams and utility owners can coordinate.
### Electronic Record Generation
Dated drone records are reliable evidence of work done, useful for billing, claims and reviews by the authority or insurers.
### Higher Transparency and Visibility
NHAI uses drone surveys to monitor highway projects consistently across contractors and regions. DATA PKT is empanelled with NHAI in three zones for monthly drone survey work.
## Operations And Maintenance
Once a road is open it needs regular inspection to stay safe. We support maintenance teams with:
Road Distress Mapping: the Quality of Roads
We convert aerial data into 3D point clouds to map stretches that need repair, and use monthly comparisons to spot potholes and encroachments early, before they become a safety problem.
Encroachment Reports
We fly the right-of-way at regular intervals and mark encroachments such as illegal structures, vegetation overgrowth or unauthorised activity on annotated images, ready for the authority to act on.
Corridor Mapping
Highways are long and narrow, so we plan flights along the corridor rather than over blocks of land. One flight plan covers the road, its right-of-way and the land on either side, and the same plan is re-flown for every repeat survey.
- Flight plans follow the alignment, so coverage is continuous with no gaps between blocks.
- Ground control points are spaced along the corridor to hold accuracy over long stretches.
- The same plan is re-flown each month, so surveys line up for comparison.
- Outputs come in the GIS and CAD formats your design and asset teams already use.
Cost Estimation: Repairs And Maintenance
Knowing the quantities before work starts lets maintenance teams budget accurately and avoid surprise costs.
Early detection means smaller repairs: defects are fixed before they spread, and the material for each repair is measured rather than guessed.
Measured cut and fill volumes mean less material wasted on each repair.
VIR (Visual Inspection of Roads)
Maintenance reports combine the latest survey with earlier flights, so you can see how each defect has developed, what it will take to fix and which stretches to prioritise.
The result is a maintenance plan based on measured data, with safer roads and fewer emergency repairs.
Bridge Inspection
Drones can inspect bridge decks, piers, bearings and abutments from angles that are hard or unsafe to reach from the ground, with little or no road closure.
High-resolution photos and video of each component give engineers a record of condition to inspect, compare between visits and use to prioritise repairs. Our guide to bridge inspection by drone explains what it can and cannot replace.
Tree Count
After construction we survey the corridor to count and map existing trees and identify suitable sites for plantation along the highway.
The report lists tree counts and proposed plantation sites, supporting compensatory plantation and environmental compliance.
## Deliverables
## Detailed Project Reporting (DPR)
Survey, site inspection, earthwork measurement and route comparison in one package: the base data a highway DPR needs. See our guide to drone surveys for highway DPRs .
## DTM
A bare-earth terrain model, with buildings and vegetation removed, generated from drone imagery or LiDAR and tied to ground control. It is the base for road levels, earthwork and drainage design.
## Contour Mapping
Contours at the interval your design needs, generated from the terrain model, for alignment, gradient and drainage design.
## Orthomosaic
A continuous, geo-referenced aerial map of the corridor stitched from hundreds of drone photos, accurate enough to measure from and overlay on design drawings.
## DSM
A surface model that includes buildings, trees and other above-ground features, used to find obstructions along the corridor and plan clearances.
## Aerial Photogrammetry and Videography
Aerial photos and video of the corridor for planning, progress reports and stakeholder presentations.
## Topographical Survey
A full topographic survey of the corridor: ground levels, features and existing road details in CAD, ready for design.
## DEM Creation
An elevation model of the corridor for alignment and gradient analysis, delivered in GIS-ready formats.
## Lidar Survey
LiDAR reaches the ground through gaps in vegetation, so it is the better choice for corridors with tree cover or hilly terrain. See LiDAR vs photogrammetry .
## Land Use Land Cover
A land use and land cover map of the corridor (farmland, built-up land, forest, water bodies) for land acquisition planning and environmental assessment.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: Can a drone survey replace a conventional topographic survey for a highway DPR?
For most corridors, a drone survey tied to DGPS ground control points gives the base topography for a DPR faster than a fully manual survey. Areas under dense tree cover, structures and cross-drainage details are usually completed with DGPS or total station on the ground. The two methods are normally combined rather than one replacing the other.
Q: What outputs does a highway drone survey give?
An orthomosaic of the corridor, a terrain model (DTM), contours, the existing road and features in CAD, and cross-sections where needed. During construction, the same corridor can be flown again for progress monitoring and video reports.
Q: How is progress on an under-construction highway monitored with drones?
The same stretch is flown at regular intervals, usually monthly, and each flight is compared with the last. This gives a visual record of progress, quantities moved and issues on site that can be shared with the authority and the contractor.
Q: What is a video project report (VPR) for a highway project?
A video project report is the monthly record of a highway stretch made from a drone flight: the video of the corridor with completion figures for each activity and site observations. Comparing it with the previous month also flags new encroachments and buildings along the corridor.
Q: How often are NHAI highway projects surveyed by drone?
Every month. NHAI has made monthly drone video recording mandatory for national highway projects during construction, operation and maintenance, and the comparative videos of the current and previous month are uploaded to its Data Lake portal.
Q: Does DATA PKT work with NHAI?
Yes. DATA PKT is empanelled with NHAI in three zones for monthly drone survey work.

# Drone Survey for Railways and Metro
In short: we carry out drone and DGPS surveys for railway and metro projects: pre-construction and DPR surveys, Engineering Scale Plans of yards, construction progress monitoring, and inspection of track, bridges and structures. Data is tied to ground control and delivered as orthophotos, elevation models, 3D models, CAD drawings and thermal data (see our railway drone inspection guide ).
Railway agencies use DATA PKT for project planning, construction monitoring and infrastructure assessment. Our survey drones with high-resolution sensors deliver centimetre-level accuracy, and our GIS specialists and pilots work to meet or beat deadlines. Deliverables include orthophotos, elevation and terrain models, 3D models and thermal data.
Our complete Aerial Inspection service checks railway tracks, infrastructure, assets, bridges, and more. Regular aerial inspections help transportation companies monitor their most precious assets and prevent calamities. Our skilled pilots can quickly collect airborne data without disrupting traffic on crowded railroad tracks while adhering to rigorous railway safety standards.

## Planning
### Pre-Construction Survey
Before a new line, yard or station is designed, we survey the candidate sites and corridors from the air to check whether the ground is suitable and what lies in the way, tied to DGPS control so the data can be designed on.
### Detailed project report
A railway DPR needs reliable base data: topography, existing features, land and quantities. We provide the survey and mapping that the DPR is built on.
### Surveying and Mapping
Photogrammetry or LiDAR, tied to DGPS ground control, gives topographic maps and 3D models of the corridor, showing terrain and obstacles before the alignment is fixed.
### Site Inspection
Repeat flights record progress, safety hazards and adherence to drawings, with dated imagery shared with the railway and the contractor.
### Earthwork Monitoring
Stockpile volumes and cut and fill quantities measured from each survey, so earthwork can be checked against the schedule.
### Route Optimization
For a new alignment we map each option with an orthomosaic, elevation model and contours, check conflicts with existing structures, and digitise revenue maps to estimate land cost alongside construction quantities.
## Construction
Project progress monitoring
During construction, regular aerial surveys keep the railway, the contractor and the consultant looking at the same up-to-date picture of the site, so delays and deviations are caught early.
- Regular aerial surveys catch delays and deviations early.
- Flights are planned to follow railway safety rules on and near the track.
- Video reports highlight unfinished work such as incomplete overbridge piers.
## Inspection
Railway bridges and buildings
Railway bridges and structures are hard and sometimes unsafe to inspect from the ground. Drones photograph them in detail without putting staff at risk, and our GIS team turns the imagery into 3D models and maps for structural assessment.
- Bridges and structures inspected in detail without staff working at height.
- Lower cost and risk than traditional access methods.
- 3D models and maps for structural assessment.
Railway track
For scheduled inspection of busy track, drones collect data quickly while following railway safety rules. The imagery is processed into orthoimagery, 3D models, point clouds and textured meshes, used to measure track and spot hazards early.
- Data collected quickly, with minimal disruption to traffic.
- Orthoimagery, 3D models, point clouds and textured meshes.
- Track measured and hazards flagged before they cause damage.
Monitor the vacant land around the railway track
We survey the land on both sides of the track to identify vacant railway land, boundaries and encroachments, and repeat the survey to track changes along the right-of-way.
- Vacant parcels and encroachments identified on both sides of the track.
- Repeat surveys track changes along the right-of-way.
- Reports show land parcels, boundaries and encroachments for land management.
## Engineering scale Planning
An engineering scale plan in railways is a detailed, technical drawing that illustrates the design and layout of railway infrastructure. This includes tracks, signals, stations, bridges, tunnels, and other related components. The purpose of such a plan is to provide a precise, scaled representation of how the railway system will be constructed and operated.
Drone survey tied to DGPS control is how we prepare ESPs. See our ESP and DPR survey page and railway yard and drainage plan case study .
### Surveying and Mapping
We survey long stretches of line with photogrammetry or LiDAR, tied to DGPS ground control, to build the maps and 3D terrain models needed to plan new routes or upgrade existing ones.
### Enhanced Accuracy
DGPS corrects the positional errors of standard GPS, so track alignment, station placement and other components can be designed on exact measurements.
### Alignment and Layout
High-precision DGPS measurements mean new track and changes to existing track are set out accurately, with fewer costly corrections on site.
### Construction Monitoring
During construction, aerial imagery and video are compared with plans and timelines, and DGPS measurements check the position of structures such as bridges and track.
### Data Integration
Combining DGPS measurements and drone imagery with other data in GIS supports route planning, environmental assessment and logistics.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: Which company does drone surveys for railway projects in India?
DATA PKT, a drone survey company in Gurugram, surveys railway yards and sections with drones, LiDAR and DGPS and prepares Engineering Scale Plans, yard plans and drainage designs. It has submitted 30 yard plans and 31 drainage plans for a railway division in eastern India and surveyed 32 yards for drainage design in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
Q: What is an Engineering Scale Plan (ESP)?
An Engineering Scale Plan is a scaled drawing of a railway station yard or section that shows tracks, points and crossings, platforms, buildings and other structures in their true positions. It is used to plan yard remodelling, new lines and other works. Drone and LiDAR surveys provide the accurate base data an ESP is drawn on.
Q: Why use drones for railway surveys?
A drone covers a yard or a long section of track quickly without staff working on the line for long periods, which improves safety and reduces block time. Survey-grade accuracy comes from ground control and RTK or PPK positioning.
Q: What railway deliverables can be produced?
Engineering Scale Plans, yard plans, drainage plans, longitudinal and cross sections, orthomosaics, terrain models, and GIS layers of railway land and assets.
Q: Can metro corridors be surveyed in dense cities?
Yes, subject to flight permissions. In crowded urban areas the drone survey is planned around permitted zones and timings and is combined with ground survey where flying is restricted.

# Engineering Scale Plans (ESP) and DPR Surveys
In short: an Engineering Scale Plan (ESP) is a scaled drawing of a railway yard or section. We prepare ESPs, and the survey data behind railway and highway DPRs, from drone survey tied to DGPS ground control, delivered in DWG, SHP, GeoTIFF and LAS formats (see what an ESP shows and drone survey for highway DPRs ).
Drone surveys are now widely used in railway engineering for planning, monitoring and maintenance. Here is how our drone data supports engineering scale planning on railways:
Surveying and Mapping
Our drones carry high-resolution cameras and LiDAR sensors to survey long stretches of railway line quickly and accurately. The data produces detailed maps and 3D terrain models for planning new routes or upgrading existing ones.
Inspection and Maintenance
Our drones inspect hard-to-reach structures such as bridges, tunnels and elevated tracks without costly, slow manual access. High-resolution and thermal imagery can show structural defects, track alignment problems and vegetation encroachment.
Monitoring Construction Progress
Drone surveys reduce the time staff spend in hazardous locations. We can also survey areas hit by landslides or floods to provide data for risk assessment and mitigation.
Asset Management
Accurate, current drone data helps railways manage track, stations and other assets, supporting planned maintenance and reducing service disruptions.
Environmental Assessment
Environmental assessment matters on railway projects, especially where lines are extended through sensitive areas. We monitor environmental impact, track change over time and support compliance with environmental regulations.
Disaster Response
After an accident or natural disaster, we can quickly survey the damage to support emergency response , decision-making and recovery work.
Cost and Time Efficiency
Drone surveys take less time and cost less than traditional survey and inspection methods. We cover large areas quickly, and our in-house processing shortens delivery.
Precision and Accuracy
Drone data tied to DGPS ground control points gives the accuracy that engineering design and approvals depend on.
Data Integration and Analysis
Our drone data is delivered in GeoTIFF, LAS, DWG and SHP formats for analysis, planning and visualisation in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Building Information Modelling (BIM).
Our drone data gives railway engineering scale planning accurate, detailed and current information, improving the efficiency, safety and cost of railway works.
## What an Engineering Scale Plan shows
An Engineering Scale Plan (ESP) is the railway's master drawing of a station yard or section, drawn to scale with every feature in its true position. Engineering, signalling, traction and operating departments all work from it, and it is the base on which yard remodelling, new lines and other works are planned, checked and approved. An ESP prepared from a drone survey typically shows:
- Track: running lines, loops and sidings, track centres, and the kilometrage along the section
- Points and crossings: every turnout with its position and direction
- Platforms and passenger structures: platform lengths and edges, foot-over-bridges, ramps, shelters and station buildings
- Crossings of the line: level crossings, road over-bridges and road under-bridges
- Traction and signalling: OHE masts and portals, signals and cabins
- Bridges, culverts and drains , with their position on the section
- Buildings and land: goods sheds, service buildings, quarters, boundary walls and fencing, and the railway land boundary
- Levels: spot levels and contours for drainage, formation and earthwork
## Where railways use ESPs and drone surveys
Railways use ESPs and drone surveys for yard remodelling and new loop lines, doubling and third and fourth lines, station redevelopment, cargo terminals and sidings, ROB, RUB and level-crossing works, yard drainage plans, and land plans and encroachments. The ESP is the base on which these works are planned, checked and approved.
Work | What the survey provides
Yard remodelling and new loop lines | The yard as it stands today, so new layouts fit the space, the structures and the levels
Doubling, third and fourth lines | A continuous strip survey of the section, with land, structures and crossings along both sides
Station redevelopment | Buildings, circulating areas, platforms and access roads mapped as one base for the architects and engineers
Cargo terminals and sidings | Site topography, approach alignment and connection to the running line
ROB, RUB and level-crossing works | Road and rail levels, approaches, utilities and nearby structures
Yard drainage plans | Ground levels and slopes, existing drains and outfalls, and the disposal point
Land plans and encroachments | The railway boundary laid over the orthomosaic, showing what stands on railway land
## How we prepare an ESP
We fix the scope with the railway, clear the flights, set DGPS ground control tied to the railway's reference benchmarks, fly the yard and process the images into an orthomosaic and terrain model. Ground survey adds rail levels and details the drone cannot see; the plan is drafted in CAD, verified on site with railway staff, corrected and submitted.
- Scope and permissions: the yard limits, the chainage and the drawing standard are fixed with the railway, and flights are cleared with the station and the airspace authority.
- DGPS control: ground control points and checkpoints are set around the yard and tied to the railway's reference benchmarks.
- Drone flights: the yard is captured with overlapping images, and with LiDAR where trees or structures hide the ground.
- Processing: the images become an orthomosaic, a surface model and a terrain model with contours.
- Ground survey: rail levels, platform heights and details the drone cannot see are measured with DGPS and total station.
- Drafting: tracks, turnouts, structures and features are drawn in CAD, in the layers and scale the railway specifies.
- Checking and submission: the drawing is verified on site with railway staff, corrected and submitted, with revisions until it is accepted.

## DPR surveys
A Detailed Project Report is only as good as the survey under it. For railway and road DPRs we provide the survey and mapping inputs the consultant and the authority need to fix the alignment, the structures and the cost:
- Topographic strip survey of the corridor, from drone photogrammetry or LiDAR with DGPS control
- Alignment options compared on the orthomosaic and terrain model
- Longitudinal and cross-sections for earthwork and formation design
- Bridges and drainage: catchments from the terrain model, waterway sections and existing structures
- Land: the corridor laid over khasra (revenue) maps, showing the land and owners affected
- Utilities and obstructions: power lines, pipelines, buildings and other features to be shifted or avoided
- Quantities: earthwork and other quantities measured from the survey data
## Why drones for railway yards
Drones capture the yard from the air, so the survey team spends far less time on or beside running lines, and flights do not need the line. One drone team captures around 5 sq km in a day, so a yard is flown in hours, and the orthomosaic and terrain model stay on file for later questions.
- Safety: the yard is captured from the air, so the survey team spends far less time on or beside running lines.
- Speed: one drone team captures around 5 sq km of survey data in a day, so a yard is flown in hours rather than surveyed over weeks.
- Little disturbance to traffic: flights do not need the line, and the ground work left is short and planned with the station.
- A complete record: the orthomosaic and terrain model stay on file, so later questions can be answered without returning to site.
Accuracy comes from the DGPS ground control and is proved on independent checkpoints. Read more in how accurate a drone survey is and what an Engineering Scale Plan is .

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is an Engineering Scale Plan (ESP)?
An Engineering Scale Plan is a scaled drawing of a railway station yard or section showing tracks, points and crossings, platforms, buildings and other features in their true positions. Railways use ESPs to plan and approve yard remodelling, new lines and other works.
Q: How does a drone survey help prepare an ESP?
A drone survey with ground control captures the whole yard as an accurate orthomosaic and terrain model in a short time. Drafters then trace tracks, structures and levels from this base, and the field team checks critical details on the ground.
Q: What survey inputs does a DPR need?
A Detailed Project Report usually needs topography of the corridor, existing features and utilities, levels for drainage and earthwork, and land details. Drone, LiDAR and DGPS surveys provide these as drawings and GIS layers.
Q: Does DATA PKT design the project itself?
We provide survey, mapping and design inputs such as drawings and plans. We do not construct projects.
Q: Which railway authorities has DATA PKT worked with?
Our railway clients include Central Railway, North Central Railway, Eastern Railway, Bridge & Roof Co. (India) Ltd and IRCON International, among other railway and metro organisations.
Q: What does an Engineering Scale Plan show?
Tracks and track centres, points and crossings, platforms, foot-over-bridges, level crossings, station buildings and other structures, OHE masts, signals, bridges and culverts, drains, the railway boundary, kilometrage and levels, all in their true positions.
Q: Do you need a traffic block to survey a station yard?
Usually not for the drone flights, which capture the yard from the air. Ground checks of rail levels and details are planned with the station and engineering staff, and kept short.
Q: How accurate is a drone survey for an ESP?
The survey is tied to DGPS ground control points and checked against independent checkpoints, and critical details such as rail levels are measured on the ground. We report the accuracy achieved on the checkpoints with every survey.
Q: In what format are ESPs delivered?
As CAD drawings in the layers and scale the railway asks for, with PDF prints, the orthomosaic, the terrain model and contours, and GIS files on request.

# Drone survey and inspection for solar, power and transmission
In short: we inspect and survey power assets by drone: transmission and distribution lines, substations, solar plants and wind farms. Radiometric thermal cameras find hotspots and defects, each tagged to its tower or string, and LiDAR maps corridors for new lines (see our transmission line and solar inspection guides). Our thermal team includes a thermographer certified to ISO 9712 Level 2.
Our drone team combines drones with advanced imaging capabilities to conduct comprehensive visual inspections of important infrastructure such as transmission and distribution lines, thermal power plants, renewable energy installations, and hydropower projects. These drones use high-resolution, infrared, and thermal sensors to detect potential problems before they escalate, resulting in lower losses, lower maintenance costs, and increased reliability. Real-time defect identification allows for timely repairs and maintenance, reducing downtime and power outages while improving operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
DATA PKT surveys and inspects power assets: transmission and distribution lines, substations and solar plants, with drone, thermal, LiDAR and DGPS methods.

## Thermal Surveys of Power Transmission and Distribution Assets
To reduce downtime caused by equipment malfunctions, modern maintenance practices emphasize the implementation of condition-based techniques for monitoring electrical assets. These methods aim to predict the deterioration of various components or vulnerable areas prone to failure.
Thermal survey is one of the most effective ways to find hot spots. Most electrical failures come from faulty components or loose connections, and infrared imaging shows them before they become failures or fire hazards.
Regular thermal surveys give asset managers early warning, so equipment can be repaired before it fails.
## Solar Power Plants
Drones are being used by solar power plants to give an airborne perspective that enables quicker diagnosis of damaged solar panels. Drones equipped with dual-mode high-end thermal cameras and ultra-high-definition video cameras with 16x zoom offer temperature differences and crisp images for quick identification of defective panels, cracks, or shadows. This technology reduces inspection time significantly, allowing for faster maintenance responses and minimized downtime. As a result, solar power plants can maintain optimal efficiency and output.
By utilizing drone technology for solar plant inspections, DATA PKT significantly reduces inspection costs by 30 to 50 percent compared to traditional methods.
Our services provide detailed topological maps and thermograms, identifying issues such as hot spots, cracked panels, and bypass diode failures, enabling prompt maintenance and optimization of solar plant performance. See how we carry out solar plant drone thermography , from flight conditions to the defect report. Deliverables: include geotagged high-resolution visible and thermal infrared images, Orth mosaics with elevation data and AI/ML-based analytics for quick analysis and provide plant efficiency reports.
## Wind Farms
Drones are becoming a crucial component of managing, operating, and preserving wind farms. Using drones instead of traditional inspection makes inspecting rotor blades simple. In one published case study, a drone inspection took about 45 minutes per turbine, against 3 to 6 hours for a rope-access inspection ( DJI Enterprise ).
Wind turbine blade inspection methods include both surface and subsurface techniques. Surface inspections use visual technologies like sensors and drones to detect fractures, erosion, lightning, and bird strikes. Early detection enables efficient corrective maintenance. Sub-surface examinations use non-destructive methods such as thermal imaging, ultrasound, and electromagnetic waves to detect structural faults in the blades' internal structure, such as damaged shear webs and bonding erosion. Internal inspections, which require professionals to physically climb into the blades, are limited due to height, safety, and efficiency limits, leaving a considerable fraction uninspected, particularly in offshore wind farms.
Our drone inspections detect a wide range of faults in wind turbine blades.
Deliverables: We provide site feasibility and topography survey reports, Higher-resolution visual inspections, Ortho-mosaic, Digital surface model, Digital terrain model with elevation data, a Contour map of the site and a 3D Model with cloud point.
## Nuclear Power Plants
Drones play a crucial role in enhancing safety and efficiency at nuclear power stations by providing an effective means of managing potential leaks and assessing equipment integrity without exposing personnel to dangerous levels of radiation. Following natural disasters and weather events, such as hurricanes or earthquakes, nuclear power stations may face structural damage or operational disruptions. In these situations, drone inspections let teams assess damage quickly without sending people into hazardous areas. This is particularly significant considering the potential catastrophic consequences of even minor damage to nuclear facilities.
Deliverable: We provide site topography survey reports with environmental impact assessment reports, Higher-resolution visual images, Ortho-mosaic, Digital surface models, Digital terrain models with elevation data, a Contour map of the site and 3D Models with cloud points.

## Hydropower Plant

## Frequently asked questions
Q: How are solar plants inspected with drones?
A drone carrying a radiometric thermal camera flies over the plant in good sunlight and records the temperature of every module. Hot spots, faulty strings, bypass diode failures and soiling show up as temperature differences and are mapped to their exact location.
Q: What is a transmission line route survey?
It is a survey of the proposed corridor for a power line to choose the best route and tower positions. Drone and LiDAR data show terrain, obstacles, crossings and clearances, which speeds up route selection and tower spotting.
Q: Can drones inspect live transmission lines and substations?
Yes. Drones inspect towers, insulators, conductors and substation equipment from a safe distance without shutting down the line, using zoom and thermal cameras.
Q: What does a solar thermography report include?
A list of every defect with its type, location, temperature difference and severity, thermal and visual images of each one, and a plant map. See our guide to solar thermography reports for details.

# Drone solar plant inspection and thermography in India
In short: we carry out solar plant drone thermography and thermal surveys of substations and roofs with radiometric cameras. The report classifies each hotspot, cell, diode or string fault and tags it to its place in the plant, so the O&M team can find and fix it ( what the report should include ). Our thermal team includes a thermographer certified to ISO 9712 Level 2, and our power-sector clients include NTPC and Adani.
## At a glance
IEC TS 62446-3
Flown to its conditions: at least 600 W/m² irradiance, cloud up to 2 okta, wind up to 4 Beaufort
ISO 9712 Level 2
Certified thermographer on our thermal team
Radiometric thermal + RGB
A temperature value for every pixel, and a visual image of each fault
NTPC and Adani
Among our power-sector clients
Every fault located
Each fault tagged to its place in the plant, so the O&M team can find it
Thermal surveys utilize unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with thermal imaging cameras to capture the infrared radiation emitted by objects and surfaces. This advanced technology enables the detection and visualization of temperature variations across surveyed areas, offering a wide array of applications in various industries.
On a solar plant, each inspection follows the steps set out in how we inspect a solar plant , from site assessment to the defect report.
## Why plant owners inspect by drone
A solar module that is ageing normally loses output slowly. A review of nearly 2,000 measured degradation rates by researchers at the US National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) found a median of 0.5 percent a year [1] . Faults behave differently. A failed bypass diode, an open string or a blown combiner fuse takes a fixed share of generation offline at once and keeps it offline until someone finds it. On a large plant, monitoring at inverter level may show this only as a small dip in a large total, without saying which string or module is at fault.
### How large the losses are
Raptor Maps, a solar inspection software company, publishes an annual Global Solar Report from the inspection data on its platform. Its 2026 report, which covers 2025, puts the average equipment-driven power loss across the sites in its data set at 5.08 percent [2] . PV Tech's coverage of the report notes that this is more than double the 2.36 percent recorded in 2021 [3] . For a site at that average, the report estimates up to US$5,070 per MW of annual revenue at risk [2] .
The same report shows where the loss sits. String faults account for 26.89 percent of the observed equipment-driven loss and combiner faults for 21.51 percent; tracker faults contribute nearly 14 percent, and inverters now account for less than a quarter [2] . String and combiner faults are among the clearest findings of a thermal flight, because a string that is not exporting runs warmer than the strings beside it.
Two cautions apply. The report gives no figures for India, so its numbers show the scale of the problem rather than predict the loss at any one plant. And revenue lost per MW depends on the tariff, so a dollar figure from other markets does not translate directly to an Indian plant.
### A small share of faults causes most of the loss
Raptor Maps' 2025 report found that issues classed as high priority were responsible for about 90 percent of the observed loss, although they were a minority of all the issues found [4] . An inspection is therefore only as useful as its ranking: the O&M team needs to fix the costly faults first, not work through a list in the order it was recorded.
### Some faults are a safety risk, not only a yield loss
The International Energy Agency's PV Power Systems programme (IEA PVPS) Task 13 review of module failures notes that a defective bypass diode or cell interconnect ribbon may possibly lead to a fire, and that hot spots can reach temperature differences of multiples of 10 K above the normal parts of the module [5] . It lists junction box failure among the most common failures seen in the field [5] . Task 13's later review of infrared and electroluminescence imaging adds that hot spots with strong local heat gradients can significantly affect module performance and, in extreme cases, lead to smouldering fires [6] .
### Why a drone rather than a handheld camera
A drone views the plant from above, within the viewing angles IEC TS 62446-3 allows, and records a radiometric image of every module in one consistent set that can be compared with the next survey. With a handheld camera, a person on foot has to walk every row and hold the camera at a usable angle to each module.
Handheld thermography works, but a plant can have tens of thousands of modules. The IEA PVPS review describes aerial infrared thermography as a cost-effective and much less time-consuming option for fault diagnosis [6] . For a side-by-side comparison of time, cost and what each method finds, see drone vs manual solar panel inspection .
Reporting and Recommendations
Each report lists every defect with its class and its position on the plant layout, with the thermal and visual images and the temperature difference to healthy modules, and a summary by block or inverter so repairs can be planned. See what a solar thermography report should include .
## When to inspect
Inspect a solar plant at commissioning or handover, in routine O&M cycles, after storms or a drop in performance, and before a warranty claim. The survey records the condition of every module, tracks changes over time, finds new faults, checks that earlier repairs worked and documents each defect for a warranty claim.
- At commissioning or handover , to record the condition of every module before the plant changes hands or the warranty period runs on.
- In routine O&M cycles , to track changes over time, find new faults and check that earlier repairs worked.
- After storms or a drop in performance , when hail, wind or an unexplained fall in yield points to damage that needs locating.
- Before a warranty claim , so each defect is documented with its class, its position and radiometric images.
Thermography is an O&M survey. Before construction, see our guide to topographic surveys for solar plants .
## Radiometric thermal and visual imaging
We use radiometric thermal cameras that record thermal images and video with a temperature value for every pixel, at centimetre-level detail. On a solar plant the inspection covers every module and string, from single cells up to whole blocks, and we support your O&M team through interpretation of the results.
Solar panel thermal imaging survey
With radiometric thermal imaging, a drone survey finds faults at cell level within a panel, panel level within a sub-array and array level within a block, faster and more safely than manual inspection. See our guide to solar thermography reports .
The ability to detect and diagnose issues with such precision enables maintenance teams to promptly enhance energy output and prevent further damage. By swiftly identifying performance faults, teams can take proactive measures to mitigate potential losses and ensure optimal operational efficiency of solar installations.
To facilitate the identification of performing panels or sub-arrays, we offer raw thermal radiometric imagery for processing. Alternatively, our expert team can handle the thermal data analysis, producing detailed hotspot reports integrated with GPS data. This comprehensive approach ensures that our clients receive actionable insights tailored to their specific needs, supporting informed decision-making and proactive maintenance strategies.
## How we inspect a solar plant
We fly to the conditions and requirements of IEC TS 62446-3, the technical specification for outdoor infrared thermography of PV modules and plants. A thermal image taken outside these conditions can hide faults or show faults that are not there.
- Site assessment and flight plan. We agree the requirements with the plant team, assess the site for areas of interest, risks and safety needs, and plan the flights for weather, flight height and coverage.
- Plant running, conditions stable. The plant is in normal operation and the flight is made in clear, steady sunlight, because a fault only shows as heat when the modules are producing power.
- Irradiance of at least 600 W/m². Irradiance in the plane of the modules is checked before and during the flight. If it drops below the minimum, flying stops until it recovers.
- Wind and cloud within limits. Cloud cover of no more than 2 okta (2/8 of the sky) and wind of no more than 4 Beaufort (about 28 km/h), so that passing shadows and wind cooling do not mask or mimic faults.
- Resolution of about 3 cm per pixel. The flight height is set so that each thermal pixel covers about 3 cm of the module, which puts roughly five pixels across each cell.
- Viewing angle above 30° to the module plane. At shallower angles the glass reflects the sky and the sun, and the temperature reading is no longer reliable.
- Radiometric camera. Every pixel carries a temperature value, so each anomaly can be measured against healthy modules and compared from one year to the next.
- Certified personnel. IEC TS 62446-3 expects the thermographer to hold a recognised certification. Our thermal team includes a thermographer certified to ISO 9712 Level 2.
- Processing and analysis. After the flight, our team processes the raw thermal data into thermal maps and analyses them for hotspots and other anomalies. Each one is classified and tagged to its place in the plant for the report.
## Solar plant defects a thermal inspection finds
Each fault has its own thermal pattern. The table shows the common ones, what usually causes them and what is usually done about them.
Defect | How it looks in the thermal image | Likely cause | Usual action | Priority
Single-cell hotspot | One cell clearly warmer than the cells around it | Cracked or damaged cell, local shading or dirt | Check the visual image; clean, or replace the module if the hotspot persists | Medium; high if very hot
Bypass diode (hot substring) | One third of the module evenly warmer than the rest | Bypass diode active or failed | Replace the diode or the module; check for a shorted diode | High
String off | A full string of modules warmer than the strings next to it | Blown fuse, open connector or other string fault | Check the fuse and connections at the combiner box | High
PID or patchwork heating | Several warm cells in an irregular, patchwork pattern | Cell degradation, potential-induced degradation (PID) | Group the affected modules by string and inverter; investigate PID | Medium
Soiling and shading | Irregular warm areas with soft edges | Dust, bird droppings, vegetation, nearby structures | Clean, trim, or plan around fixed shade | Low to medium
Junction box or connector | A small, very hot point at the junction box or cable | Loose, corroded or poorly crimped connection | Repair promptly; it can be a fire risk | High
## What you receive
Deliverable | What it shows | Format
Raw radiometric thermal imagery | Thermal images in which every pixel carries a temperature value, for your own processing | Agreed per project
Geotagged thermal and visual images | The thermal image and the RGB image of the same position, so heat and visible damage can be compared | Agreed per project
Thermal map of the plant | The raw thermal data processed into thermal maps of the plant, showing where each hotspot and anomaly is | Agreed per project
Hotspot report | Each anomaly classified and tagged to its place in the plant, integrated with GPS data | Agreed per project
## What the inspection covers, and what a drone thermal survey does not replace
A drone thermal survey is a screening method for faults that make heat. It is one part of a plant's testing and maintenance regime, not the whole of it. The lists below describe general industry practice, not the scope of any one contract.
### What a thermal flight covers
A thermal flight screens every module in the area flown for faults that make heat: hot cells and hotspots, strings that are not exporting, active or failed bypass diodes, overheating junction boxes and connectors, and soiling and shading. The RGB image taken with each thermal image shows broken glass, frame damage, debris and vegetation at the same position.
- Modules. Hot cells and hotspots, broken glass once it causes heating, and the patchwork heating typical of potential-induced degradation (PID), on every module in the area flown.
- Strings. Whole strings that are not exporting, which run warmer than the strings beside them and usually point to a blown fuse or an open connector at the combiner box.
- Bypass diodes. A substring, typically one third of the module, running evenly warmer than the rest when its diode is active or has failed.
- Junction boxes and connectors. Overheating that shows through the module at the junction box position, or on cables and connectors visible from above.
- Soiling and shading. Soft-edged warm patches from dust, bird droppings, vegetation and fixed shade, so cleaning and trimming can be planned.
- Visual condition. The RGB image taken with the thermal image shows broken glass, frame damage, debris and vegetation at the same position.
### What a drone thermal survey does not replace
- Electrical tests. IEC 62446-1 sets Category 1 tests for all grid-connected PV systems, including earth continuity, polarity, string open-circuit voltage and current, functional and insulation resistance tests [7] . A thermal image measures none of these.
- I-V curve tracing. IEC 62446-1 lists the I-V curve test and infrared inspection as separate Category 2 tests [7] . Thermography shows that a string is likely losing power; an I-V curve trace measures how much.
- Electroluminescence (EL) imaging. EL shows micro-cracks and other defects within the cell material [6] , including cracks that do not yet cut a cell off or make heat.
- Inverter internals and enclosed equipment. A drone sees the outside of an inverter, combiner box or transformer. The components inside need their own inspection and maintenance on the ground.
- Confirming the cause. A thermal anomaly tells the ground team where to look. Confirming the cause, for example whether a diode is shorted or open, needs a check at the module.
A good inspection plan uses the drone to find and map every fault that makes heat, then sends the ground team only where the drone points. Read the full comparison in drone vs manual solar panel inspection .

Drones and sensors are chosen to suit each survey: camera, LiDAR, thermal or multispectral.
## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is a drone thermal survey?
A drone thermal survey uses an infrared camera on a drone to measure surface temperature across a site. Faults that change temperature, such as failing solar cells, loose electrical joints or water ingress, become visible in the thermal image.
Q: When should a solar thermal inspection be flown?
In clear, steady sunlight with the plant operating, usually around midday. The widely used standard for aerial thermography of PV plants, IEC TS 62446-3, sets a minimum irradiance of 600 W/m² on the modules.
Q: What defects can thermal drones find in a solar plant?
Hot spots and cell cracks, bypass diode faults, open or disconnected strings, junction box overheating, potential induced degradation patterns, and soiling or shading.
Q: What is the difference between radiometric and non-radiometric thermal cameras?
A radiometric camera records a temperature value for every pixel, so each defect can be measured and compared. A non-radiometric camera only shows relative hot and cold areas. Inspection reports need radiometric data.
Q: What does a solar thermography report include?
Each defect with its class, its position on the plant layout, the thermal and visual images, and the temperature difference to healthy modules, with a summary by block or inverter so repairs can be planned.
Q: Does the plant need to shut down for a drone thermal inspection?
No. The plant must be running, because a fault only shows as heat when the modules are producing power. The flight is made during normal operation, in steady sunlight, and is coordinated with the plant team so that no blocks are switched off or curtailed.
Q: Is a drone thermal inspection compliant with IEC TS 62446-3?
Only if it meets the standard's conditions, resolution, personnel and reporting requirements; a drone does not make an inspection compliant by itself. The conditions include irradiance of at least 600 W/m² on the modules, cloud cover of no more than 2 okta, wind of no more than 4 Beaufort and a resolution of about 3 cm per pixel, and the thermographer should hold a recognised certification such as ISO 9712.
Q: What can a drone thermal inspection not find?
Cell cracks that have not yet cut a cell off, which electroluminescence (EL) imaging shows; the exact power a string is losing, which an IV-curve trace measures; and faults inside combiner boxes and inverters, which need a physical check on the ground.
Q: How does a drone thermal inspection differ for rooftop and ground-mounted plants?
The flight conditions are the same, but the site is not. On a rooftop the flight has to be planned around the building, its occupants, nearby structures and local airspace rules, and the modules often sit at a low tilt close to roof equipment that can give off heat or cast shade. Rooftop arrays are smaller, so they can usually be covered in a short flight. Ground-mounted plants are larger and open, so the work is planned block by block, and access, dust and vegetation between rows matter more.
Q: Can plants with single-axis trackers be inspected by drone?
Yes. The modules change angle through the day, so the flight is planned around the tracker position: the camera must view the modules at more than 30° to their plane, and the sun's reflection moves as the trackers turn. A row stuck at the wrong angle or left in stow is itself a fault worth recording. Raptor Maps' 2026 Global Solar Report found that tracker faults contributed nearly 14 percent of the equipment-driven loss in its data set.
Q: How soon after commissioning should a solar plant be inspected?
As soon as it is exporting at normal load in steady sunlight, because thermography needs current flowing through the modules to show faults. A baseline survey at commissioning or handover, while the EPC contractor is still responsible for defects, records the faults present from the start so they can be raised with the contractor or the module supplier.
Q: What weather cancels or pauses a solar thermal flight?
Anything that takes the plant outside the conditions of IEC TS 62446-3: irradiance below 600 W/m² on the modules, cloud cover above 2 okta or wind above 4 Beaufort. Rain or wet modules, heavy haze or dust that cuts the sunlight, and passing cloud that makes irradiance change quickly also stop useful work, because a module takes several minutes to settle to a new temperature after the light changes. In India the monsoon leaves fewer usable days, so flights are planned for clearer seasons or for clear spells between rain.
Q: What does the O&M team receive after the inspection?
In general, a list of anomalies they can work from: each one with its class, its place in the plant, the thermal and visual images, the temperature difference to healthy modules and a priority, with a summary by block or inverter. A plant map with the anomalies marked helps crews find each one on the ground. The raw radiometric images can also be handed over, so the plant's own team or a third party can analyse them again.
Q: How are anomalies from a solar thermal inspection prioritised?
By what they risk and what they cost. Hot points at junction boxes, connectors and cables come first, because they can be a fire risk. Faults that take a large share of generation offline, such as strings that are not exporting or failed bypass diodes, come next. Single-cell hotspots, PID patterns and soiling are ranked by their temperature difference to healthy modules, since a large temperature difference usually means a large power loss, and by how many modules are affected. Raptor Maps' 2025 Global Solar Report found that high-priority issues caused about 90 percent of the observed loss, so the ranking matters more than the length of the list.
Q: How often should a solar plant be inspected by drone?
At least once a year as part of routine O&M, plus a baseline at commissioning or handover, a survey after hail, high winds or an unexplained drop in yield, and one before a warranty claim. Older plants, plants with a history of faults and plants in hot, dusty climates gain from more frequent surveys, because comparing radiometric data from one survey to the next shows faults that are spreading.
Q: Do the modules need to be cleaned before a thermal flight?
No, but it helps to know when they were last cleaned. Soiling shows in the thermal image as soft-edged warm areas, and heavy soiling can hide other faults beneath it. Flying soon after a cleaning cycle makes it easier to tell soiling apart from defects; flying before cleaning shows where soiling is costing the most.
See it in practice: how we checked drone thermography data from a 340 MWp solar plant before analysis , and our guide to what a solar thermography report contains .

# LiDAR Drone Survey
In short: DATA PKT is a LiDAR drone survey company in Gurugram. We fly drone LiDAR over highway, railway and power line corridors , mines and terrain under vegetation, and deliver classified point clouds, DTM, DSM and contours ready for CAD and GIS. LiDAR survey cost is set by the area or corridor length, point density, ground control, vegetation and deliverables ( how survey cost is worked out ).
Drone LiDAR survey uses a laser scanner on a drone to capture accurate, detailed 3D data of the ground and everything on it. It is faster and cheaper than traditional survey, especially in difficult or inaccessible terrain.
At DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics, we provide secure drone operations to ensure quick data collection, low-cost aerial lidar scanning, and top-notch positional accuracy. We specialize in providing professional drone LiDAR surveying services to meet the diverse needs of our clients. Here's how we deliver value through our service:
Data collection
To collect data, LiDAR uses a specialized sensor that emits pulses of light and measures the time it takes for these signals to bounce back, allowing it to create incredibly detailed 3D maps of land and terrain with pinpoint accuracy.
Our drones carry survey-grade LiDAR sensors that record dense, accurate 3D points of the ground, vegetation, buildings and other features.
Customised Survey Planning
Our team works closely with clients to understand their project requirements and objectives. We design customised survey plans tailored to each project, considering factors such as area coverage, point density, and resolution to ensure optimal data quality and relevance.
Efficient Data Acquisition Our pilots fly pre-planned flight paths, which lets us cover remote or difficult terrain safely and at lower cost than ground survey.
Data Processing
After data capture, we process the raw LiDAR data using specialised software to generate detailed point clouds. Our team applies sophisticated algorithms to clean, filter, and classify the point cloud data, enhancing its accuracy and usability for various applications.
The LiDAR chain. A single pulse can return several times as it passes through vegetation. The last returns reach the ground, which is why LiDAR can map terrain under trees.
## Lidar Deliverables
Depending on the particular objectives and specifications of a project, our drone LiDAR (light detection and ranging) technology offers a broad range of outcomes. Our LiDAR outputs offer the potential to provide extremely accurate and detailed topography data that is useful for a wide range of applications across various sectors. The following are potential deliverables we provide:
Deliverable | What it shows | Format
Classified point cloud | Every laser return as a 3D point, classified as ground, vegetation, buildings or wires | LAS, LAZ
DTM | The bare ground, with buildings and vegetation removed | GeoTIFF
DSM | The ground together with everything on it, such as buildings and trees | GeoTIFF
Contours and cross-sections | Lines of equal height and sections cut from the terrain model | DWG, DXF, SHP
Orthomosaic | A measurable true-colour map from the camera flown with the scanner | GeoTIFF; KMZ for quick viewing
Volume calculations | Stockpile and earthwork volumes measured from the point cloud | Agreed per project
Accuracy report | Checkpoint errors (RMSE) in X, Y and Z | PDF
## Orthomosaic map
Drone photographs are corrected for distortion and merged into a precise orthomosaic. Every pixel carries X and Y coordinates, so distances and areas can be measured directly from the map.
## 3D Point Cloud
The LiDAR sensor fires laser pulses and records each return. The drone's GNSS receiver and IMU record its position and orientation for every pulse, so each return is georeferenced into a point with X, Y and Z coordinates. The points are then classified into ground, vegetation, buildings, wires and other classes , giving a precise model for measuring lengths, heights, areas and volumes.
## DSM
A DSM (Digital Surface Model) is the first surface the laser meets: the ground together with the tops of vegetation, buildings and other above-ground features. It is built from the highest LiDAR returns, so each cell stores X, Y and the elevation of the top surface at that position.
## DTM
A DTM (Digital Terrain Model) is the bare-earth surface. It is built only from the points classified as ground, with vegetation, buildings and other above-ground features removed. Because some laser pulses reach the ground through gaps in vegetation, LiDAR can model the terrain under tree cover. Each cell stores X, Y and the ground elevation.
## Contour map
Contour lines are generated from the DTM at the contour interval the project needs, showing the shape of the ground across the surveyed area.
## Volume Calculations
Drone LiDAR can be used to calculate the volume of materials, such as soil, rock, and gravel, with a high degree of accuracy. This information can be used for a range of applications, including mining, construction, and environmental studies.
## LIDAR is used for Infrastructure
Lidar drones play a pivotal role in infrastructure development and maintenance. They are used to create precise 3D models of roads, bridges, and other critical infrastructure. These models aid in design, construction, and monitoring, ensuring safety and efficiency.
Topographic analysis and site monitoring
On construction sites, LiDAR gives engineers a detailed 3D model of the ground, showing topography, hazards and unstable areas before work starts, which informs foundation types, excavation and site layout.
Better knowledge of the site means better-matched foundations, less excavation and safer, faster construction.
Infrastructure monitoring
For pipelines, turbines and power lines, LiDAR drones let inspectors find cracks, deformation and other defects remotely, without hazardous and slow in-person inspection.
The data helps maintenance teams prioritise repairs, plan schedules and reduce the risk of unexpected failures and downtime.
## Mining

LiDAR technology is used in mining locations to analyse slope stability. By identifying high walls and unstable slopes, it lowers the chance of collapse. This proactive approach to safety reduces the possibility of catastrophic accidents, which can be especially serious in mining environments, and improves worker safety.

Mineral mapping and mineral exploration can be assisted by LiDAR technology. It provides geologists with useful information for planning future exploration endeavours and streamlining mining operations by helping them locate possible mineral deposits and map those that already exist. The sustainable management of mineral resources depends on this data.

For accurate estimation of the amount of material placed in mining operations, LiDAR drones are essential. Workers in forestry can increase timber output and support sustainable forest management techniques by enhancing tree density.

Repeat LiDAR surveys during construction produce 3D models of the site before and during works, giving contractors, engineers and architects one shared picture to plan from.
With access to precise topographic data, stakeholders can proactively identify potential issues, monitor progress, and make data-driven decisions, ensuring projects are completed on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards. The adoption of LiDAR drones in construction site monitoring has led to a significant reduction in errors, improved communication among stakeholders, and increased efficiency. By harnessing the power of LiDAR technology, construction professionals can drive innovation, ensure successful project outcomes, and set new benchmarks for excellence in construction. ## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is a drone LiDAR survey?
LiDAR sends laser pulses from the drone and measures their return to build a dense 3D point cloud of the ground and everything on it. Because some pulses pass through gaps in vegetation, LiDAR can map the ground surface under trees.
Q: When should I choose LiDAR over photogrammetry?
Choose LiDAR for corridors and sites with vegetation, for power lines and for very detailed terrain. Photogrammetry is usually more economical for open ground and gives a true-colour orthomosaic. Many projects use both.
Q: What deliverables come from a LiDAR survey?
A classified point cloud (ground, vegetation, buildings, wires), a digital terrain model, a digital surface model, contours and cross-sections, in formats ready for CAD and GIS.
Q: How accurate is drone LiDAR?
Accuracy depends on the sensor, flying height and ground control. Survey-grade drone LiDAR checked against ground control typically reaches a few centimetres vertically on hard surfaces.
Q: What does a LiDAR drone survey cost in India?
It depends on the job, so each survey is quoted for its site. A corridor is priced per km and a compact site per hectare or acre. The price then moves with the point density needed, the ground control, how much vegetation has to be classified out, and the deliverables, from a ground model alone to full CAD drawings.
Q: What do you need from me for a LiDAR survey quote?
A KML or map of the area or corridor, the accuracy and point density required, the coordinate system, the deliverables and the deadline.
