# Drone Photogrammetry
In short: drone photogrammetry turns overlapping aerial photos, tied to DGPS ground control points, into measurable maps. Our in-house GIS team delivers orthomosaics, DSMs, DTMs, contours and point clouds for highway, railway, mining, urban and environmental projects. Accuracy depends on ground sample distance and control (see our accuracy guide and GSD calculator ).
Photogrammetry builds a map of an area from many overlapping photographs. A camera on a drone or aircraft points straight down or at a steep angle and captures images from different positions, each overlapping the next. The overlap is what allows measurements to be calculated from the images.
The variation in perspective among the photos is key to this process. By analyzing how specific points or features appear differently in each image, photogrammetry software can perform "image matching." This technique correlates corresponding points in multiple photos, enabling the creation of a detailed 3D model from a sequence of 2D images.
We handle the full photogrammetry workflow: flight planning, image capture tied to DGPS ground control points, and processing by our in-house GIS team. Outputs include orthomosaics, DSMs, DTMs, contours and point clouds for infrastructure, environmental and urban planning work.
At DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics, we help with the following photogrammetry steps:
## Data Acquisition
Planning and Preparation
- Define project objectives and requirements.
- Identify survey area and assess potential obstacles.
- Determine optimal flight path and altitude.
- Ensure 80% image overlap for accurate orthophoto creation.
- Check weather conditions and obtain necessary permits.
Equipment Setup
- Ensure drone and camera are in good working condition.
- Calibrate drone sensors and cameras.
- Install and configure additional hardware (e.g., GPS).
Camera Model Optimization
Camera calibration calculates camera specifications using photos of a 3D object with a geometrical pattern (e.g., checkerboard). Calibration types include Full, Field, Self, and Auto.
- Full calibration sets up a specific camera calibration project.
- Field calibration optimizes the camera during normal project processing.
- Self-calibration adjusts camera parameters for each photo individually.
- Auto calibration integrates with Smart Orientation for field calibration.
## GCP (Ground control points)
Ground control points (GCPs) are marked points on the ground with surveyed coordinates. Because each one can be located precisely in the aerial images, a few GCPs are enough to tie a large survey area to real-world coordinates.
Any feature that is clearly visible in the photos can serve as a GCP. Most are checkerboard-style targets, because the pattern leaves no doubt about the exact centre of the point.
### Is it always necessary to use GCP?
Not always. If the drone does not have RTK or PPK, we always use GCPs. With an RTK or PPK drone, GCPs add little to accuracy but still serve as independent accuracy checks . Without GCPs a survey can still give a usable model, but it may lack correct scale, orientation or absolute position.
GCPs have long been standard in aerial mapping, though RTK and PPK drones are changing how many are needed.
GCPs and RTK or PPK geotags allow the result to be checked for accuracy.
### The difference between GCP, Automatic and Manual tie points
GCP coordinates are fixed on the ground with instruments such as DGPS and total stations.
Automatic tie points are features that the software detects in several overlapping photos. They are used to stitch the images together.
Any immediately identifiable place that appears in several photos, such as the corner of a building or a road, can be used as a manual tie point.
Manual tie points can assist in enhancing a project's relative accuracy, but they can't help with absolute precision because their location in space isn't known.
## Flight Execution
- Conduct a pre-flight check to verify all systems are functioning correctly.
- Launch the drone and follow the planned flight path, adjusting altitude and camera settings as needed.
- Capture overlapping aerial images with sufficient ground coverage and detail.
- Maintain communication and monitor the drone's position and battery life throughout the flight.
- Ensure the drone returns to the home point or a safe landing location with ample battery reserve.
- Post-flight inspection to assess drone condition and review any captured data for quality.
- Transfer and back up all aerial images and data to a secure storage location.
- Analyze the captured images to create a detailed map or 3D model of the surveyed area.
- Download and back up all captured images and flight data immediately after landing.
- Regularly check the weather conditions and adjust the flight plan if necessary.
## Data Processing
- Transfer the captured imagery to a computer or processing device.
- Use specialized photogrammetry software to stitch together the individual images into a cohesive mosaic.
- Apply algorithms to triangulate image features and generate a dense point cloud representing the surveyed area.
- Generate orthomosaics, digital surface models (DSMs), and other derived products from the processed data.
- Validate the accuracy of the generated models by comparing them with ground control points (GCPs) or known reference data.
- Perform quality checks on the orthomosaics and DSMs to identify and correct any artifacts or inconsistencies.
- Export the processed data into various formats suitable for different applications and software platforms.
- Integrate the geospatial data with GIS software for further analysis and visualization.
The photogrammetry chain. Each output is built from the one before it, and the checkpoint QA at the end tests the whole chain against points the adjustment never saw.
## Data Quality Control and Analysis
- Validate the accuracy and completeness of the generated 3D models and maps.
- Conduct any necessary adjustments or corrections to improve the quality of the data.
- Perform measurements, analysis, and interpretation of the photogrammetric outputs to extract relevant information.
- Share the validated models and maps with stakeholders for feedback and further insights.
- Use the extracted measurements to inform project design and planning decisions.
- Document the methodologies and workflows used in the photogrammetric process for reproducibility and future reference.
- Train client teams to use the photogrammetry outputs.
- Keep processing methods and software up to date to improve quality and turnaround.
## Deliverables
## Orthomosaic map
Drone photographs are corrected for distortion and merged into an orthomosaic map. Each pixel carries 2D geographic coordinates (X, Y), so horizontal distances and areas can be measured directly from the map.
## 3D Point Cloud
Drone images are processed into dense point clouds in which every point has coordinates (X, Y, Z) and colour. They allow horizontal and vertical distances, areas and volumes to be measured.
## DSM
A DSM (Digital Surface Model) represents the ground together with everything on it, such as buildings and vegetation. In a DSM built from drone images, each pixel holds its position (X, Y) and the elevation (Z) of the highest point at that location.
## DTM
A DTM (Digital Terrain Model) represents the bare ground, with buildings and vegetation removed . It is produced from low-altitude imagery taken with a geometrically calibrated camera, and each pixel stores X, Y and the ground elevation (Z).
## Contour map
Contour maps are generated from the DTM or DSM at the interval the project requires, showing the shape of the ground across the surveyed area. See how to choose the interval in our guide to topographic and contour survey by drone .
## 3D Textured Mash
A 3D textured mesh built from drone imagery shows the site's surfaces, walls and edges in detail, giving a complete view of the area for analysis and project planning.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is drone photogrammetry?
Photogrammetry builds maps and 3D models from many overlapping aerial photos. Processing software matches points across the photos to produce an orthomosaic, a surface model and a 3D mesh.
Q: How accurate is drone photogrammetry?
With RTK or PPK positioning and well-placed ground control points, drone photogrammetry typically reaches a few centimetres of accuracy. The ground sample distance (GSD), which depends on camera and flying height, sets the level of detail.
Q: What is a ground control point (GCP)?
A GCP is a marked point on the ground whose coordinates are measured with DGPS. GCPs tie the drone map to real-world coordinates, and independent checkpoints are used to prove the final accuracy.
Q: What file formats will I receive?
Usually GeoTIFF orthomosaics and elevation models, contours and features in DWG or DXF, GIS layers as shapefiles or GeoPackage, and point clouds in LAS or LAZ.

# Drone Survey for Mining
In short: we survey mines by drone to measure stockpile volumes, map pits, benches and haul roads, and monitor progress without sending staff into hazardous areas. Imagery tied to ground control is processed into DTMs, DSMs, 3D models and volume reports for each survey, so quantities can be checked against the mine plan (see survey deliverables explained ).
DATA PKT uses drone surveys to support mining operations, including inventory and stockpile management and hotspot detection. From aerial imagery we produce digital terrain models, digital surface models and 3D terrain models of mine sites, from which mining block depths and elevations can be measured without sending staff into hazardous or remote areas. High-resolution imagery supports inspection, mapping and ongoing monitoring of difficult terrain. This helps mine operators reduce delays, improve site safety, plan resource use and manage risk.
Exploration and Discovery stage
Development
Production
Reclamation stage
## Stage 1: Exploration and Discovery stage
Mineral exploration is the search for evidence of mineralisation in the surrounding rock. Geological information from many sites is combined and projected across a wider area to build a geological picture. Exploration of new regions grows with the demand for resources.
Drone surveys have changed how mineral exploration is carried out.
Drone surveys provide a base image of the region's geology at the start of exploration. Each later stage of work in the area builds on and relates back to this initial dataset, making exploration more efficient and accurate.
## Stage 2: Development Stage
Using a drone, DATA PKT assists in optimising the following processes throughout the mining development phase:-
### Haulage Road Optimization
A haul road is a type of road in the mining industry used to transport heavy and bulky materials by haul trucks. It is sometimes referred to as a haulage road or a haul track.
Material hauling accounts for a significant portion of a mine's expenses. Well-designed and maintained haul roads make transport safer and directly reduce cycle times, fuel use, tyre costs and overall cost per tonne moved.
Drones support haul road work through accurate mapping, time-critical surveys and quick road inspections, helping manage road maintenance over the long term.
### Surveying and Mapping
Conventional surveying needs careful measurement, planning and preparation, which slows data collection. A drone survey gathers the same data in much less time and needs half the field labour of a conventional survey.
### Tailings dam monitoring
Tailings dams are common at metallurgical and coal mines. Built of earth, they can cover several square kilometres and hold the contaminated by-products of mining. Monitoring them by drone means fewer staff need to enter unsafe areas, as the survey is flown from a line-of-sight distance, away from harmful chemicals and dust.
## Stage 3: Production Stage
### Stockpile management and calculation
Stockpile management reduces environmental impact and supports regulatory compliance in mining and construction. Covering, grading and vegetation control sediment run-off from soil stockpiles and protect nearby waterways. It matters most for erodible materials, where it prevents soil loss, contamination and hazards to surrounding areas.
DATA PKT measures stockpiles by drone and shares the results with stakeholders, giving a clear record of inventory and reducing waste. Regular quarry surveys show changes early, so issues can be addressed before they affect safety or output. Accurate volumetric measurements improve planning and forecasting.
## Stage 4: Land Reclamation
Reclamation of mined land is the process of restoring it to the condition it was in before mining. When you restore land, you are minimizing the negative environmental consequences of mining. Reforestation and new development are the most typical methods of reclamation.
Drone surveys track extraction progress and material movement, showing how much work remains and when reclamation can begin. Repeat aerial surveys are a quick and reliable way to collect this data.
### Benefits of using drones in the mining sector:-
Site Safety Management
Mining sites have unstable sections and rugged terrain where safety comes first. Drones capture photogrammetric data of mines that is processed into digital elevation and surface models, supporting better site management and task planning.
Automated Inspection
Automated drone flights can inspect blast sites without putting people at risk, and reduce the manpower needed for mine inspection. The data collected is processed into orthomosaic maps that give an up-to-date view of large areas.
Site Monitoring And Mapping
DATA PKT drones monitor mine sites with high-quality sensors, giving cost-effective access to current data. UAVs can monitor deep tunnels that cannot be inspected manually, helping with site surveillance and the detection of leaks that could endanger people, so corrective action can be taken quickly.
Mine Survey Using Lidar
LiDAR (light detection and ranging) surveys of mine pits produce accurate topographic maps of mining operations. Drone-mounted LiDAR gives precise data on embankment slopes and unstable ground, while surveyors stay clear of difficult terrain.
Volume Calculation
Volume calculations show the cost and efficiency of machines and mining methods. Installing RTK-GPS equipment on site can put surveyors at risk, so drone-derived digital terrain models (DTM) are used to calculate volumes instead.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: How are stockpile volumes measured with drones?
The drone maps the stockpiles and the software builds a 3D surface. Volumes are calculated against a base surface, which is faster and safer than walking the pile with a survey instrument.
Q: How often should a mine be surveyed by drone?
Many mines fly monthly or quarterly so that excavation, dumping and stock figures can be compared period by period. The frequency depends on how fast the site changes and reporting needs.
Q: Can drones map active pits safely?
Yes. The drone collects data from the air, so surveyors do not need to approach unstable faces or work near moving equipment.
Q: What mining outputs are typical?
Orthomosaics, terrain models, contours, pit and dump boundaries, volume reports, haul road profiles and change-detection maps between surveys.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: How are drones used in water resources projects?
Drones survey canals, rivers, embankments and reservoir shorelines to produce terrain models, cross-sections and maps for design, repair and monitoring.
Q: Can a drone survey measure underwater depth?
Standard drone cameras do not see through water, so depth is measured by a bathymetry survey with an echo sounder. The two datasets are merged into one model of the banks and the bed.
Q: What outputs help canal design and maintenance?
Longitudinal and cross sections, bank and bed levels, contour maps , encroachment mapping and orthomosaics of the canal corridor.
Q: Can drones help with flood studies?
Yes. An accurate terrain model of the catchment or floodplain is a key input to flood modelling and planning embankments and drainage.

# Bathymetry Survey
In short: we map the beds of rivers, lakes, reservoirs and coastal waters with drone-mounted sonar, each depth reading georeferenced by high-precision GPS, adding LiDAR and cameras where needed. Our GIS engineers and hydrographic specialists deliver depth contours, depth and volume data, point clouds, 3D surface models and reports for planning, design and monitoring. See water resources surveys .
DataPKT provides drone-based bathymetry services, using drones fitted with specialised sensors and imaging systems for underwater mapping. We work on coastal zone management, hydroelectric, environmental monitoring and infrastructure projects.
Drone surveys can be deployed quickly over water bodies of different sizes and conditions, with little disturbance to the aquatic environment. They capture underwater terrain at high resolution, giving clients accurate bathymetric data for planning and design.
Our GIS engineers and hydrographic specialists process and analyse the survey data into reports and deliverables. All survey operations follow strict safety and operating protocols.
Whether you need underwater topography for project planning or ongoing monitoring of water resources , contact DataPKT to discuss your bathymetric survey.
## High-Resolution Mapping
High-resolution mapping produces detailed maps of underwater terrain. Sonar and GPS systems mounted on drones record precise depths and the shape of the bed. The service works as follows.
Data Collection
- Sonar Technology Drones equipped with sonar sensors emit sound waves that travel through the water and bounce back after hitting the seabed, lakebed, or riverbed. The time taken for the sound waves to return is used to calculate the depth of the water at various points.
- GPS Integration High-precision GPS systems onboard the drones ensure that each depth measurement is accurately georeferenced, allowing for the creation of detailed spatial maps.
Data Processing
- Depth Contours The collected depth data is processed to generate depth contours, which are lines connecting points of equal depth. These contours help in understanding the variations in underwater terrain.
- Feature Identification Detailed maps can highlight specific underwater features such as trenches, ridges, and submerged objects, providing valuable information for various applications.
Applications
- Environmental Studies High-resolution maps aid in the study of aquatic habitats, helping to monitor and protect ecosystems.
- Engineering Projects Accurate topographical data is crucial for planning and constructing underwater structures like bridges, pipelines, and docks.
- Navigation Mariners use these maps to navigate safely, avoiding underwater hazards.
Advantages
- Precision and Detail High-resolution mapping provides a high level of detail, which is essential for accurate analysis and decision-making.
- Efficiency Drones can cover large areas quickly, significantly reducing the time and cost compared to traditional survey methods.
## 3D Modeling
3D modelling builds three-dimensional representations of underwater environments, giving a clearer picture of the underwater landscape than flat maps.
Data Collection and Integration
- Multi-Angle Scanning Drones perform multiple passes over the survey area, collecting data from different angles. This multi-angle approach ensures that all features are captured accurately.
- Integrated Sensors Alongside sonar, drones can be equipped with additional sensors like LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) and high-resolution cameras to enhance the detail and accuracy of the models.
Model Generation
- Point Cloud Creation The data collected is used to create a point cloud, a set of data points in a three-dimensional coordinate system representing the underwater terrain.
- Surface Reconstruction Advanced software processes the point cloud to generate a 3D surface model, which can be textured and colored to reflect the actual appearance of the seabed.
Applications
- Visualization 3D models provide an immersive view of the underwater environment, useful for presentations, education, and stakeholder engagement.
- Simulation and Analysis Engineers and scientists can use these models for simulations, such as predicting the impact of construction projects on the underwater landscape.
Advantages:
- Enhanced Understanding 3D models offer a more intuitive and comprehensive view of the underwater environment compared to traditional 2D maps.
- Versatility These models can be used in various software applications for further analysis, virtual reality experiences, and detailed planning.
## Coastal and Shoreline Surveys
Tracking shoreline erosion shows how coastlines change over time. Monitoring erosion patterns and shoreline positions lets authorities plan coastal management and defence measures to protect vulnerable communities. Habitat mapping complements this by surveying sensitive habitats such as coral reefs, seagrass beds and mangrove forests .
This shows scientists which areas need protection or restoration. Together, erosion monitoring and habitat mapping give a fuller picture of coastal change and support conservation plans that balance human needs with the environment.
## Environmental Monitoring and Assessment
Water quality monitoring records parameters such as temperature, pH and turbidity alongside depth measurements, describing the physical and chemical condition of a water body and helping locate pollution sources. Sediment transport studies explain how sediment moves in rivers, lakes and coastal areas.
Analysing sediment distribution and movement shows how waterways and coastlines are shaped. This informs measures to control erosion and siltation and reduce the effect of human activity on aquatic ecosystems. Combined with water quality data, it supports effective management of water resources.
## Infrastructure Planning and Inspection
Before building bridges, piers or underwater pipelines, a pre-construction survey of the seabed, water depth and surroundings lets engineers fit the design to site conditions and reduce risk. Regular inspections are also needed for existing structures such as dams, levees and seawalls.
Inspections identify damage, deterioration and maintenance needs, so repairs can be made before failures occur. Together, site assessments and inspections help keep underwater infrastructure safe and serviceable.
## Flood Risk Management
Floodplain mapping identifies areas vulnerable to flooding, taking account of topography, hydrology and storm patterns, and forms the basis of flood risk management plans. Assessing flood defences such as levees and barriers checks that they can still protect against floods.
Flood defence assessments identify strengths and weaknesses in these structures and recommend upgrades or repairs. Combined with floodplain mapping, they help communities manage flood risk and protect lives, property and infrastructure.
## Aquaculture
Fish farm surveys assess water quality, seabed topography and other factors to find the best locations for fish cages, supporting growth while limiting environmental impact. Environmental impact studies show how aquaculture affects the marine ecosystem.
These studies monitor water quality, sedimentation and biodiversity, and assess the risk of disease and parasite transfer between farmed and wild fish. Regular studies let fish farms address problems early and operate sustainably.
## Archaeological Surveys
Underwater archaeology requires precise location and mapping of sites such as shipwrecks and submerged settlements. Detailed maps and 3D models record these sites accurately, preserving historical and cultural information and helping researchers understand past events and human activity.
Accurate mapping also allows site condition to be monitored over time, supporting conservation of these cultural resources and the study of sites that were previously hard to reach.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is a bathymetry survey?
A bathymetry survey measures the depth and shape of the bed of a river, reservoir, lake or canal, usually with an echo sounder linked to GNSS positioning.
Q: Why combine bathymetry with a drone survey?
The drone maps banks and dry areas, and bathymetry maps the bed under water. Together they give one continuous terrain model for design, capacity and siltation studies.
Q: What can bathymetry data be used for?
Reservoir capacity and siltation studies, dredging volumes, river training and bridge design, intake and outfall design, and flood modelling.
Q: What are the typical deliverables?
Depth points, a bed surface model, contours, cross-sections and capacity tables, in CAD and GIS formats.

# Drone Survey for Agriculture
In short: we survey farmland with drones carrying RGB, multispectral, hyperspectral, LiDAR and thermal sensors. ## Mid-Season
### Hyperspectral based species mapping
Utilizing hyperspectral sensors on drones enables precise species mapping by capturing spectral signatures. These sensors detect unique wavelengths reflected by various vegetation types, aiding in accurate species identification. Data processing techniques analyse spectral information to map species distribution and abundance. This approach offers efficient and non-invasive monitoring of ecosystems for biodiversity conservation and management.
Hyperspectral drone surveys support ecological research and environmental monitoring.
### Crop health and stress analysis
Our multispectral and thermal drone surveys capture detailed imagery of fields to monitor crop health and detect pests, disease and nutrient deficiencies. Multispectral sensors can show disease and stress at an early stage, sometimes before it is visible on the ground or in standard colour images. The processed data feeds irrigation monitoring, crop health monitoring and treatment planning.
Using RGB sensors, crop variability can be assessed using the visual atmospheric resistance index (VARI); however, NIR and multispectral sensors are better at detecting and distinguishing crop stress using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE) is also often used in conjunction with multispectral data, offering more accurate crop health analysis in later growing stages. Thermal cameras can also be used to determine crop water stress by picking up variations in temperature within a crop, indicating irrigation issues.
Plant health algorithms explained
Healthy plants reflect light differently than unhealthy plants. This allows us to pick out plants that may be under stress from disease, pests, dehydration, etc. This is done by using plant health algorithms such as the Visual Atmospheric Resistance Index (VARI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE). These algorithms are the most commonly used for agricultural purposes.
VARI was designed to be used with RGB sensors and measures how green an image is. Healthy plants tend to reflect more green light and less red light. This allows VARI to highlight areas where less green light is being reflected, suggesting plant stress.
NDVI was designed to be used with NIR and multispectral cameras and measures the ratio between NIR and red being reflected from a plant. Plants that are healthy should be absorbing red light for photosynthesis and reflecting more NIR than stressed plants, allowing for this algorithm to indicate the health of plants.
NDRE was designed to be used as an index for multispectral cameras and measures the ratio between NIR and red edge being reflected from a plant. This algorithm is typically better in the later growth stages of crops, as Red edge is absorbed less than red light by surface leaves, giving a better overview of plant health when plant canopies are dense. NDRE gives a picture of leaf chlorophyll content, which is a good indicator of foliar nitrogen levels
## UAV SERVICES FOR IRRIGATION
DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics provides aerial surveys for irrigation planning and monitoring, and for detecting irrigation problems. The work focuses on the land and soil factors that govern water management, using multispectral, hyperspectral, LiDAR and thermal sensors with GIS analysis to improve irrigation practice.
Soil moisture estimation is a key service. High-resolution aerial imagery and suitable sensors show soil moisture across fields, so farmers can schedule irrigation to avoid both water waste and crop water stress, improving yield and quality.

Visual Inspections
Visual inspection is the most common way to find leaks in a water pipeline system: pipelines, valves and other components are checked for signs of damage or leakage. Drones with high-resolution cameras supply real-time aerial imagery for these inspections.
This shows signs of deterioration or leakage, such as cracks, corrosion or misalignment, as soon as they appear. Our drone imagery and video help to:
- Monitor regions that are difficult to access without putting staff in danger
- Reduce the amount of time spent on site inspections
- Evaluating the quality of the water and locating areas of high contamination in order to implement targeted interventions.
- Detect cracks, corrosion, misalignment and other signs of deterioration or leakage from real-time aerial imagery.
- Cover the whole pipeline network, including areas that are hard or unsafe for staff to reach.
Multispectral imaging (MSI)
Multispectral imaging records several wavelengths to analyse different parts of a scene, such as vegetation, soil and water.
Drones with multispectral sensors help with leak detection, hydrological mapping and surveying in the following ways:
- Analysis of the vegetation: Extra soil moisture can make vegetation greener, which may indicate a leak.
- Moisture detection: The presence of moisture can be determined by using multispectral imaging. Water leaks have the potential to change the amount of moisture that is present in the soil.
- Change detection: We are able to identify possible leaks and track the course of breaches that are already present by comparing multispectral data at regular intervals.
By detecting, monitoring and fixing leaks in water distribution systems early, these surveys help conserve water and limit damage to infrastructure.
Lidar Technology
LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) uses laser pulses to produce detailed 3D maps of a water distribution system.
Combining drones and LiDAR allows us to:
- Measure the pipelines and their surroundings accurately.
- Detect small elevation changes or ground deformation that may indicate leaks, using high point-density data that gives a precise picture of the pipeline network.
- Detect leaks early to reduce water loss.
- Identify potential obstructions or encroachments near the water distribution system that could impact its functionality or integrity.
- Assess the overall condition of the infrastructure, including the presence of corrosion, cracks, or other signs of deterioration.
Thermal Imaging
Thermal imaging uses infrared cameras to detect temperature changes on the surface of water pipelines and the surrounding ground.
When drones with thermal cameras are flown over a water distribution system:
- Warm areas can indicate leaks, since escaping water is at a different temperature from the surrounding soil.
- Temperature contrast shows the position and extent of leaks before they get worse.
- Detect leaks early from temperature variations on pipeline surfaces and the surrounding ground.
- Assess how severe and extensive leaks are from temperature contrast, so they can be fixed before they escalate.
- Locate leaks promptly to reduce water loss, structural damage and service disruption.
Soil moisture estimation
Using drones equipped with thermal sensors, our service provides swift and precise analysis of soil moisture. By capturing thermal images from aerial perspectives, we identify and map fluctuations in soil temperature, allowing for accurate evaluation of moisture levels. This data assists farmers in optimizing irrigation techniques, improving crop vitality, and maximizing harvest yields. Our advanced drone technology streamlines operations, reducing expenses and time investments while delivering crucial agricultural management insights.
Thermal imaging maps variation in soil temperature across a field, which shows how moisture is distributed and where irrigation is needed.
This is faster and cheaper than traditional soil assessment and supports decisions that affect yield.
Farmers get timely moisture maps that support efficient water use and consistent yields.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is NDVI?
NDVI (Normalised Difference Vegetation Index) is a measure of plant health calculated from red and near-infrared light. Healthy vegetation reflects more near-infrared, so stressed areas show up clearly on an NDVI map.
Q: What camera is used for crop health mapping?
A multispectral camera that records near-infrared and other bands as well as visible light. Hyperspectral cameras record many narrow bands for research-level analysis.
Q: What can drone maps do for a farm or plantation?
Show crop stress and variation across fields, map field boundaries and drainage, count plants or trees, and help plan inputs where they are needed.
Q: Is drone mapping useful for agricultural research?
Yes. Repeated multispectral flights give consistent, measurable data on plots over the season.

# Drone Survey for Oil and Gas
In short: we provide thermal and visual inspection of plants and pipelines, pipeline surveillance, aerial videography for change detection, aerial topographical surveys for greenfield projects, construction progress monitoring and sensor-based leakage and risk investigations, supporting upstream, midstream and downstream operations. A drone inspects the pipeline from the air while it stays in service, and flare stack checks can be done without shutting down production. Our thermal team includes a thermographer certified to ISO 9712 Level 2.
At DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics, we specialize in providing a comprehensive range of services tailored to the needs of the oil and gas industry. Our offerings include thermal and visual plant and pipeline inspections, pipeline surveillance, drone-based aerial videography for change detection, aerial topographical surveys for greenfield projects, drone-based real-time construction progress monitoring, and sensor-based leakage and risk investigations.
The oil and gas industry is divided into upstream, midstream and downstream sectors. Upstream covers exploration, drilling and production of crude oil and gas from natural reservoirs. Midstream covers transport by pipeline, tanker or barge, and storage. Downstream covers refining into petroleum products and their distribution to industrial, commercial and residential users.
We support each stage of this value chain with drone surveys and thermal inspections , helping operators work safely and meet regulatory requirements.
Upstream
Midstream
Downstream
## Upstream
Upstream work includes site selection, surveys, drilling, exploration and production of crude oil and gas. Drones make this traditionally slow, manual process faster and more accurate in the following ways:
### Provide up-to-date data at every stage.
- Thermal sensors and cameras on drones provide data for identifying suitable transfer routes and related infrastructure.
- During construction, managers can remotely supervise progress using real-time video feeds from drones, facilitating timely decision-making and project oversight.
- Designers can check work in progress against the plans and see where changes are needed.
- Drones support predictive maintenance by regularly collecting data on issues such as leaks and corrosion, so maintenance can be planned before failures occur.
- Data relayed from drones in real time shortens the gap between collection and action, so problems can be dealt with promptly.
## Midstream
Midstream is the transport of crude oil and gas from upstream sites to downstream processing and storage, by pipeline, barge or tanker. Pipelines may run long distances above ground or underwater, and the product often needs secure storage during treatment and before onward transport.
Secure storage is needed throughout midstream operations, to deal with transport delays and surplus stock, and to hold product between treatment and onward transit.
- Infrastructure for midstream operations also encompasses storage facilities such as tanks, terminals, and depots, strategically located along transportation routes to facilitate smooth transitions between different modes of transportation and accommodate fluctuations in demand.
- Midstream operations are critical to a reliable energy supply and are subject to strict safety and environmental regulations covering the transport and storage of crude oil and gas.
## Downstream
Standing at the conclusion of the cycle, downstream serves as a link between oil and gas businesses and end consumers (B2B, B2C & B2G). At this stage, crude oil and raw natural gas are refined to produce end products such as gasoline, jet fuel, heating oil, natural gas, LPG, and other petrochemicals.
Because downstream is closest to the end user, considerable people and resources go into delivering products on time and with minimal environmental impact. Industrial waste must also be disposed of safely.
### Drones help in midstream and downstream operations in the following ways:
Pipeline Inspections
The inspection of pipelines is one of the most important applications of drones in the oil and gas industry. Drones provide an aerial perspective that allows for comprehensive analysis of pipeline conditions without having to shut down the pipeline. A pipeline inspection drone can spot environmental encroachments, physical damage, corrosion, leaks, and spills.
Gas Flare Stack Inspections
Gas flare stacks are used to burn off waste gases from oil and gas production. Flare stack inspections are critical to maintaining safety and compliance. A drone can capture high-resolution images and thermal imaging to detect leaks, gas combustion, and other potential safety hazards. Through drone inspections, maintenance checks can be done without having to shut down production.
Power Line Inspections
Power lines are critical to the oil and gas industry. Drones can provide effective visual inspections and thermographic imaging to detect damage, wear and tear, and hot spots on power lines. Inspections can be done much more efficiently than traditional methods, reducing costs and minimising safety risks.
Oil Rig Inspections
Drones can inspect oil rig platforms, derricks, and equipment. With infrared imaging, drones can detect potential equipment failures and cracks that might not be visible from the ground. A drone inspection of drilling platforms increases cost-effectiveness, efficacy, and safety.
Tank Inspections
Tanks are crucial elements in the oil and gas industry. Routine inspections are necessary to detect leaks, surface corrosion, or other damage to the tank. Drones can detect surface level changes, leaks, and other issues that might not be visible to the naked eye. A drone inspection of tanks reduces safety risks and maintenance costs.

Q: Can a pipeline be inspected by drone without shutting it down?

## Water Resource Management
Our drone surveys of water bodies cover water quality monitoring, depth measurement, pollutant detection, irrigation system management and flood risk assessment. Each is described below.
Water Quality Monitoring
Drones fitted with suitable sensors and cameras can assess several water quality parameters, including:
- Temperature: Thermal sensors detect temperature variations in water bodies.
- pH Levels: Specialized sensors measure the acidity or alkalinity of water.
- Turbidity: High-resolution cameras assess water clarity by detecting the presence of suspended particles.
- Chemical Contaminants: Drones can identify pollutants such as heavy metals, nitrates, and phosphates through spectral analysis.
Regular monitoring helps in maintaining water safety standards and addressing contamination issues promptly.
Depth Measurement
Using sonar and LiDAR, drones can measure the depth of water bodies. This data is used for:
- Navigational Charts Providing accurate and up-to-date information for safe navigation.
- Sediment Analysis Understanding sediment accumulation patterns for dredging purposes.
- Habitat Studies Assessing the aquatic environment to support marine life research and conservation efforts.
Depth measurement via drones is faster and safer compared to traditional methods.
Pollutant Detection
Drones with multispectral and hyperspectral sensors help detect pollutants in water bodies. They can:
- Identify Oil Spills Detecting the presence and extent of oil contamination.
- Chemical Spills Spotting areas affected by chemical spills from industrial discharges.
- Nutrient Loads Measuring levels of nitrogen and phosphorus that contribute to algal blooms.
Early detection lets pollution be contained and corrected sooner, limiting environmental damage.
Irrigation System Management and Flood Risk Assessment
Drones help manage irrigation systems and assess flood risk through:
- Irrigation Audits: Monitoring the distribution and efficiency of irrigation systems to optimize water usage and enhance crop yields.
- Flood Mapping Creating detailed topographic maps to predict flood-prone areas.
- Flood Monitoring Providing real-time data during flood events to support emergency response and evacuation planning.
- Erosion Control Monitoring riverbanks and coastal areas to identify erosion patterns and implement preventive measures.
## Soil and Land Degradation
Detailed topographic data from drone surveys shows where soil is being eroded and how fast. Comparing high-resolution imagery and 3D models from repeat surveys identifies vulnerable areas, measures erosion rates and supports erosion control measures.
Land Degradation Monitoring
Drone surveys map degraded land, including loss of vegetation, soil fertility and biodiversity, and track changes over time to help identify the causes. The data supports targeted restoration plans and shows whether land management measures are working.
Desertification Processes
In areas at risk of desertification, drones monitor changes in land cover and vegetation health. Multispectral and thermal images show early signs such as reduced vegetation cover and more exposed soil, so action can be taken in time.
Land Restoration Projects
On restoration projects, drones record the existing land condition and identify areas that need work. Repeat surveys then track progress, show the effect of the work and confirm whether objectives are being met.
## Air Quality Monitoring
For air quality surveys, our drones can carry sensors that measure the following parameters:
Particulate Matter (PM) Detection
- Drones equipped with particulate matter sensors can accurately measure PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 levels in the atmosphere. This data is vital for assessing air pollution levels and understanding health risks associated with fine particulate matter.
CO2 and Gas Monitoring
- Gas sensors on our drones measure carbon dioxide (CO2) and other gases such as methane (CH4), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and ozone (O3), to evaluate greenhouse gas emissions and air quality compliance.
Environmental Pollutant Assessment
- Drone sensors can detect pollutants including volatile organic compounds (VOCs), airborne toxins and industrial emissions , helping to identify pollution sources and check regulatory compliance.
Real-Time Data Collection
- Drones cover large areas quickly and give real-time air quality readings, supporting prompt decisions in environmental management and emergency response.

# Hyperspectral and Multispectral Surveys
In short: we fly drone hyperspectral and multispectral surveys for agriculture, forestry, environmental monitoring, mineral exploration and resource management. A multispectral camera records a few predefined bands, typically visible (RGB) and near-infrared, which is enough for vegetation indices such as NDVI; a hyperspectral sensor records many narrow, contiguous bands, giving a detailed spectral signature for each pixel. Outputs include spectral signatures, vegetation indices, mineral maps and environmental indicators, with a report and maps that set out the findings.
Drone hyperspectral survey is an advanced method of remote sensing that employs unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with hyperspectral sensors. These sensors capture detailed imagery across numerous narrow spectral bands, allowing for precise data collection on the electromagnetic spectrum reflected or emitted by objects on the Earth's surface. This technology provides extensive and specific information that can be analyzed to gain insights into diverse phenomena such as vegetation health, mineral composition, and environmental changes.
DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics provides drone hyperspectral surveys planned around each client's requirements, from data collection through to analysis.
Our hyperspectral surveys capture imagery across many spectral bands for detailed analysis of environmental and geological features: vegetation health, mineral composition, land use patterns and change over time. The high-resolution data supports planning in agriculture, forestry, environmental monitoring and resource management.
Planning and preparation
Our skilled team collaborates closely with clients to grasp their precise goals and needs for the hyperspectral survey. We conduct detailed site assessments to identify the best flight routes, sensor setups, and parameters for data collection.
During site assessment we look at terrain, environmental conditions and project scope, and use these to set flight paths, sensor configuration and data collection parameters.
Planning each survey around the client's objectives and any regulatory requirements sets the base for reliable data collection and analysis.
Data Acquisition
We fly UAVs carrying high-resolution hyperspectral sensors that capture imagery across many spectral bands. Pilots follow pre-planned flight routes for complete coverage of the survey area.
Planned flight paths and consistent sensor settings give complete, accurate data that can be analysed in detail.
The data collected supports applications including environmental monitoring, agriculture and mineral exploration.
Data Processing and Analysis
We process raw hyperspectral data with specialised software, using spectral unmixing, classification and feature extraction. Outputs are matched to each client's needs and include spectral signatures, vegetation indices, mineral maps and environmental indicators.
These methods let us interpret the data reliably and extract the information relevant to each project.
Spectral signatures characterise materials, vegetation indices show plant health, mineral maps show geological composition and environmental indicators track ecological conditions, giving users in agriculture, environmental monitoring and resource management data they can act on.
Interpretation and Reporting
We interpret the analysed data and turn it into clear findings and recommendations, presented in reports and maps that clients can act on.
Benefits of Our Drone Hyperspectral Survey Service:
- Precision and Accuracy: Hyperspectral sensors on our UAVs, with careful processing, give precise and accurate results.
- Efficiency and cost-effectiveness: Drone-based surveys offer a faster and more cost-effective alternative to traditional methods, reducing time and resource requirements.
- Insights and Intelligence: Detailed spectral information supports analysis and interpretation for a wide range of applications.
- Environmental Monitoring and Resource Management: Our service supports environmental monitoring, land management, agriculture, forestry, mining, and other industries where detailed spectral information is critical for decision-making.
## Multispectral
Multispectral surveying is an advanced remote sensing technique employing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with multispectral sensors. These sensors capture imagery across several predefined spectral bands, providing detailed data on the reflectance properties of Earth's surface objects. This technology enables precise analysis of phenomena such as vegetation health, soil composition, and environmental dynamics.
We provide drone multispectral surveys planned around each client's requirements. Our UAVs capture high-resolution imagery across several spectral bands for detailed assessment of environmental and geological features.
Survey Planning
We collaborate closely with our clients to comprehend their goals and establish the parameters for the multispectral survey. Our team of specialists develops tailored flight plans to guarantee thorough coverage of the designated area and enhance the accuracy and quality of the data collected.
We first agree the objectives, parameters and scope of the survey with the client, then prepare flight plans that give full coverage of the target area.
Flight plans take account of terrain, environmental conditions and project goals, so the data collected is reliable and meets the client's analytical needs.
Our multispectral surveys support agriculture, environmental monitoring and land use planning.
Data acquisition
Our drones carry multispectral cameras that capture high-resolution images in several spectral bands, recording visible (RGB) and near-infrared (NIR) bands together to analyse vegetation health, moisture content and other variables.
Recording RGB and near-infrared bands at the same time gives the data needed to assess vegetation condition, moisture and other factors affecting crops and the environment.
The imagery supports decisions in agriculture, forestry and natural resource management.
We keep our multispectral equipment and methods up to date so the data supports sound land management and environmental decisions.
Data Processing and Analysis
After the survey, we process the multispectral imagery with specialised software. Our analysts derive vegetation indices such as NDVI, chlorophyll levels and soil properties, and deliver reports and maps to support crop management, irrigation, pest monitoring and related work.
Typical outputs include NDVI and other vegetation index maps, chlorophyll content and soil characteristics, presented as reports and visualisations.
These outputs feed directly into planning and resource allocation in agriculture and environmental management.
Reporting
From the survey results we prepare reports aimed at improving crop yields, reducing input costs and managing risk, and we work with clients to turn the findings into practical actions.
We aim to provide dependable multispectral surveys that help clients improve productivity and manage land sustainably.
Our recommendations are based on careful analysis of the survey data and agreed with the client.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is the difference between hyperspectral and multispectral drone surveys?
A multispectral camera records a few predefined bands, typically visible (RGB) and near-infrared, which is enough for vegetation indices such as NDVI. A hyperspectral sensor records many narrow, contiguous bands, giving a detailed spectral signature for each pixel, which helps tell apart plant species, minerals and materials that look alike in fewer bands.
Q: What deliverables do you provide from a hyperspectral survey?
We process the raw data with spectral unmixing, classification and feature extraction, and deliver outputs matched to the project: spectral signatures, vegetation indices, mineral maps and environmental indicators. These come with a report and maps that set out the findings and recommendations in a form your team can act on.
Q: What are hyperspectral and multispectral drone surveys used for?
Common uses are crop and vegetation health, soil and moisture assessment, irrigation and pest monitoring, forestry, mineral composition mapping and exploration, land use mapping and environmental monitoring. Multispectral surveys suit routine crop and vegetation checks, while hyperspectral surveys suit work that needs finer spectral detail, such as species or mineral mapping.
Q: What is NDVI and what does a multispectral survey show?
NDVI (Normalised Difference Vegetation Index) compares the near-infrared and red light reflected by plants; healthy vegetation reflects more near-infrared. From multispectral imagery we derive NDVI and other vegetation index maps, chlorophyll content and soil characteristics, delivered as reports and maps for crop management, irrigation and pest monitoring.
Q: How do you plan a hyperspectral drone survey?
We first agree the objectives and scope with the client, then assess the site's terrain, environmental conditions and any regulatory requirements. From that we set flight paths, sensor configuration and data collection parameters, so the whole area is covered with consistent sensor settings and the data can be analysed reliably.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: What can be delivered by drone?
Drones can carry medicines, vaccines and blood samples between healthcare facilities, medical equipment and supplies to disaster-hit areas, food, water and aid where roads are damaged, letters and packages to remote areas, and small tools and equipment around construction sites. What a given flight can carry depends on the drone and the route.
Q: Is drone delivery allowed in India?
Drone operations in India are governed by the Drone Rules, 2021 , administered by the DGCA, and all our flying follows DGCA drone rules. Under these rules, airspace is divided into green, yellow and red zones, and flights in yellow or red zones need prior permission, so the route and site decide what approvals a delivery needs.
Q: Which sectors can use drone delivery?
Drone delivery is used in retail and local stores, food and grocery delivery, healthcare, logistics, construction and infrastructure, agriculture, postal services, and humanitarian aid and disaster relief. In each case the benefit is avoiding road delays and reaching places that are hard or unsafe to reach by vehicle.
Q: Can drones deliver to remote or hard-to-reach areas?
Yes. Drones can reach isolated locations where conventional delivery is impractical, such as difficult terrain or areas cut off after a disaster. Service is kept consistent within safe flying limits, which means weather and airspace conditions decide whether a flight goes ahead.

1. Search and Rescue
Drones are widely used in search and rescue because they provide information quickly. From above, they help locate missing people in hard-to-reach terrain such as hills, or in areas hit by floods, landslides, earthquakes and other disasters, where fast action saves lives.
Advantages of DATA PKT drones in search and rescue:
- Drones are able to reach a crisis situation faster than manual search and rescue efforts. UAVs aid rescue crews in saving lives by giving them quick access to reliable data in real time.
- Drones let rescue teams operate with fewer people and less equipment, making better use of scarce resources.
- Drones simplify the planning and execution of difficult missions, and allow SAR operations to be carried out safely across inaccessible terrain.
2. Firefighting
Drones add to firefighters' existing tools such as ladders, fire engines and specialist gear. They help plan and run operations by gathering aerial data quickly and at low cost. During disasters, drone data is used to locate people in homes and cars, speeding up rescue operations.
### Benefits
- Drone swarms for fire suppression are a concept in which drones fight wildfires or support conventional firefighting. Each drone carries a payload of 5 to 50 kg, and the swarm works as a single system, covering its tasks across a grid. The concept offers clear advantages over helicopters and aircraft used in conventional aerial firefighting.
- Aerial information from UAVs guides the response that protects people and property. Drones can scan large areas quickly to locate firelines, assess the danger and direct crews.
- Firefighters use UAVs to collect data quickly and safely after floods, earthquakes and storms. Incident commanders and emergency managers use this data to assess the impact on communities, infrastructure and natural assets.
3. Security
### Using Drones In Border Security
Flying at 100 feet or more, drones can cover large areas and detect activity that fixed or mobile ground sensors would miss, especially in remote or mountainous areas. Drone monitoring adds surveillance beyond physical barriers such as fences. Drones can enter areas too dangerous for people and are quicker and cheaper to deploy than helicopters, helping security services protect international borders.
### Using Drones For Crime Control
Real-time video and autonomous drones help law enforcement agencies prevent crime. Drones also help investigate crime scenes and give a remote aerial view of possible bomb threats, showing investigators details they might miss in a routine inspection.
4.Crowd Monitoring
- Drones give crowd control teams a wider view of large gatherings and real-time data for monitoring. They can zoom in on a specific area, showing the team what is happening on the ground.
- During riots and protests, this information helps commanders make key decisions. Better situational awareness lets teams respond to emergencies quickly and manage crowds more effectively.
- Drones are a low-cost way to carry out aerial surveillance. Sending a manned helicopter is expensive and slow, and may not suit situations that need a quick response.
- Drones can save lives. They carry different payloads depending on the task, operated from a safe distance by a single police officer. This is useful in high-risk situations such as counter-insurgency and hostage rescue, where officers can act without putting their own lives at risk.
5. Disaster Management
Drones support disaster management during earthquakes, wildfires, tsunamis and floods. They allow quick assessment of affected areas, carry essential items into difficult terrain to support government response, and collect aerial data that helps plan mitigation and future responses. By reducing risk to personnel and providing reliable data, they help decision-makers act quickly and soundly.
- Drones help save lives during earthquakes, wildfires, tsunamis, floods and other natural disasters, and can fly in difficult weather.
- UAVs facilitate the transportation of necessary items in challenging terrain, aiding government departments' disaster response procedures.
- Aerial data collected after a disaster helps develop mitigation strategies for future responses.
- Drones reduce risk to responders and provide reliable data, so decision-makers can act on sound information.

## Forest mapping
Drones fitted with cameras and other sensors collect high-resolution imagery for detailed forest maps. These maps are used to track changes over time, identify deforestation or illegal logging, and study tree health and growth.

Wildlife Monitoring

This is especially useful for animals that are hard to track on foot. Cameras and other sensors on the drone record behaviour, count individuals and detect movement patterns.

## Deliverables
## Aerial Imagery
We deliver high-resolution aerial photographs covering the whole site from different angles. The images record the site's features, structures and surrounding landscape, helping archaeologists understand its layout and context.
## Orthomosaic Maps
We create orthomosaic maps by stitching together hundreds or thousands of aerial images and removing distortion, so the site's terrain and features are shown accurately. These geometrically corrected maps are used for measurement, planning, analysis and site management.
## Topographical Data
We generate Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and Digital Terrain Models (DTMs) from aerial survey data. A DEM represents ground surface elevation, and a DTM shows the bare terrain with buildings and vegetation removed. These datasets support terrain analysis, slope calculation and hydrological modelling for site research and management.
## 3D Models
We build detailed 3D models of archaeological sites from aerial survey data. The models show elevation changes, structures and landscape features, letting researchers explore and analyse a site virtually.
## LiDAR Data
We produce accurate 3D terrain maps showing surface features and anomalies, including buried structures and features hidden beneath vegetation or soil cover. They give archaeologists a clear picture of the site's topography.
## Thermal Imaging Data
We analyse temperature variations across a site to pinpoint subsurface anomalies that may be archaeological features. These anomalies mark targets for further investigation, such as buried structures or artefacts.
## Aerial Photography and Videography
We provide aerial photographs and videos that record site conditions, erosion and any looting or encroachment. During excavation we also supply live or recorded aerial footage for documentation and on-site coordination.
## Regular Surveillance Reports
We provide regular reports from surveillance flights over archaeological sites, recording any changes in site condition, new risks or significant developments so they can be acted on early.

Our drone surveys, tied to DGPS ground control points, map sites accurately, locate buried structures and record ancient landscapes.

Drones cover large areas quickly, producing complete datasets with less fieldwork.

Our drones collect data without disturbing delicate sites, protecting cultural heritage for future study.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: Can a drone survey find buried archaeological features?
Drones can point to likely features. LiDAR produces 3D terrain maps that reveal structures and landscapes hidden by vegetation or soil, and thermal imaging picks up temperature differences that can indicate features below the surface. Q: What deliverables do you provide for an archaeological drone survey?

Q: Can you survey remote or difficult archaeological sites?
Yes. We choose drones and sensors suited to dense forest, mountains and desert, so remote or inaccessible sites can still be surveyed. Surveying from the air also avoids ground access that could damage sensitive archaeological landscapes.
Q: What is the difference between a DEM and a DTM?
A Digital Elevation Model (DEM) represents the elevation of the ground surface, while a Digital Terrain Model (DTM) shows the bare terrain with buildings and vegetation removed. Both are generated from aerial survey data and support terrain analysis, slope calculation and hydrological modelling of a site.

Home / Drone survey cost
Pricing guide
# What does a drone survey cost in India?
Six things decide the price of a drone survey. Here is how each one moves it, why per-acre rates mislead, and what to send for an accurate quote in one reply.
Short answer: area sites such as land parcels, mines and solar plants are quoted per acre or hectare; highways, railways, canals and power lines are quoted per km. Within either, the price is set by the accuracy you need, the ground control, the terrain, the deliverables and the location. Send the site and outputs for an exact quote.
## The six things that decide the price
Factor | What raises the cost | What lowers it
Area or length | Small, scattered sites (fixed mobilisation is spread over little area) | Large blocks and long corridors flown in one visit
Accuracy and GSD | Tighter accuracy needs lower flights, more photos and more processing | Planning-level accuracy at a larger GSD
Ground control | Many GCPs and checkpoints measured with DGPS | RTK or PPK drones, which need fewer GCPs
Terrain | Dense vegetation ( LiDAR or ground survey needed), steep hills, water | Open, accessible ground
Deliverables | CAD drawings, ESPs, cross-sections, classified point clouds, reports | Orthomosaic and elevation model only
Location and permissions | Remote sites, yellow or red airspace zones needing permission | Green-zone sites near our teams
Ground control points tie the map to real coordinates. Their number is one of the biggest cost drivers.
## Why per-acre rates mislead
A per-acre figure hides what is being delivered. One firm's rate may cover only a processed map; another's includes DGPS control, an accuracy report and CAD drawings. Compare quotes on the same GSD, the same number of control points and checkpoints, and the same list of files.
Corridors also behave differently from blocks: a 20 km highway is priced by length and width, not by acres. On a solar plant, for example, a topographic survey and a solar plant drone thermography inspection are different jobs with different outputs.
## Drone survey or ground survey?
For medium and large sites, a drone survey is usually faster and cheaper than a full ground survey, and it captures everything, not just the points a surveyor chose to measure. Ground survey still wins on very small plots and under dense tree cover, and the two are often combined. See drone survey vs DGPS and total station .
## Get an accurate quote in one reply
Send us these and we can quote without a site visit in most cases:
- A KML, KMZ or map of the site or corridor (or start and end chainages)
- The accuracy you need, or what the survey is for (planning, DPR, design, progress)
- The coordinate system and height datum, if fixed
- The deliverables: map, terrain model, contours, CAD drawings, ESP, report
- The deadline, and whether it is a one-off or a monthly survey
- Any access, security or airspace constraints you know of
Not sure what accuracy you need? Use our GSD calculator , or read how accurate a drone survey is .
Send us the site KML or chainage and the outputs you need. We reply with a scope and quote.
Send an enquiry WhatsApp +91 8448559100
## Frequently asked questions
Q: What is the cost of a drone survey per acre in India?
There is no honest single rate. Price per acre falls as the area grows, rises with tighter accuracy and more ground control, and depends heavily on the deliverables: an orthomosaic alone costs far less than CAD drawings or an Engineering Scale Plan. Share the area and outputs and we will quote for your site.
Q: Is a highway or pipeline survey priced per km or per acre?
Per km. A corridor survey is priced by its length and the width of the band to be mapped, with the accuracy, ground control and drawings on top. Per-acre pricing is used for compact sites such as land parcels, mines, plants and townships.
Q: What drives drone survey cost for land surveying?
Four things: the size and shape of the land, the accuracy needed (which sets the flying height and the number of ground control points), whether trees or buildings hide the ground, and the outputs, from a simple map to a surveyed CAD drawing with boundaries and levels.
Q: Is a drone survey cheaper than a conventional survey?
For medium and large areas and long corridors, usually yes, because a drone captures the whole site in a short time with a small team. On very small plots, or under dense trees, a ground survey can be cheaper or necessary.
Q: Why do two quotes for the same site differ so much?
Mostly because they are not for the same work. Check the GSD, the number of ground control points and checkpoints, whether an accuracy report is included, and exactly which drawings and files will be delivered.
Q: Does a monthly survey cost the same every month?
The first month carries the planning work. Later months repeat the same flight plan, so they are simpler to run.
Q: What do you need from me for a quote?
A KML or map of the site or corridor, the accuracy needed, the coordinate system, the deliverables, the deadline and any access or permission constraints.

# Drone, LiDAR and GIS data processing for survey and engineering firms
DATA PKT's in-house GIS team in Gurugram turns drone imagery, LiDAR point clouds and survey data into classified point clouds, terrain models, GIS layers and CAD-ready drawings for projects across India, and offers remote processing to firms outside India.
In short: we are a GIS mapping company in Gurugram with an in-house team working in ArcGIS, QGIS and AutoCAD. We build GIS layers from our own drone and LiDAR surveys or from your data, overlay them on revenue and forest maps, and deliver files your engineers can use directly. For firms outside India we offer remote GIS data processing and dedicated offshore seats.
## Drone and LiDAR data processing
Survey and engineering firms that capture their own drone or LiDAR data can hand the processing to us and get back outputs their drafting and design teams can use. The same team processes the data from our own surveys: we have 20+ pilots and have captured 3 lakh+ km of highway data in six years.
- Photogrammetry processing: drone images tied to ground control and processed into orthomosaics, dense point clouds and surface models
- Point cloud classification: LiDAR and photogrammetric point clouds classified to ASPRS LAS classes such as ground, vegetation, buildings and water, or to the class list your project uses (see point cloud classification explained )
- DTM and DSM: bare-earth terrain models from the classified ground points, and surface models that keep buildings, trees and structures
- Contours generated from the terrain model at the interval your drawings need
- Orthomosaics for base maps, feature extraction and GIS layers
## CAD and GIS deliverables for survey and engineering firms
We deliver files that open directly in your CAD and GIS software. Our team works in ArcGIS, QGIS and AutoCAD.
- LAS/LAZ: classified point clouds
- GeoTIFF: orthomosaics, DTM and DSM
- DWG: contours, topographic drawings and features extracted for design teams
- SHP: GIS layers with attributes to your schema
We also deliver in geodatabase, GeoPackage, KML/KMZ or DXF, in the coordinate system, projection and height datum you specify, with layer naming and attribute schemas to your template. Every job is checked against the QC rules agreed at the start.
## How a processing job works
You hand over the raw images or point clouds, the ground control and checkpoint coordinates, the coordinate system and height datum, and the outputs you need. We process the data, check the results against the ground control and independent checkpoints, and deliver the files in the agreed formats with the checkpoint results.
- Data handover: you share the raw images or point clouds, the ground control and checkpoint coordinates, the coordinate system and height datum, and the outputs and formats you need. When we fly the site ourselves, our surveyors measure the ground control with DGPS.
- Processing and QC: we process the data and check the results against the ground control and independent checkpoints, along with the QC rules agreed at the start.
- Delivery: you receive the files in the agreed formats, with the checkpoint results, ready for your drafting, design or GIS team.
## GIS services for projects in India
- GIS layers from drone and LiDAR surveys: orthomosaics, elevation models and contours brought into GIS with roads, structures, utilities, drainage and land use mapped as layers
- Drone maps on khasra (revenue) maps: current ground conditions laid over plot boundaries, so land acquisition and right-of-way planning start from facts
- Forest diversion and approval maps: KML, KMZ and shapefiles of the project boundary and affected land, prepared for forest and other clearances
- Corridor and asset mapping for highways, railways, transmission lines, canals and pipelines
- Land-use and land-cover mapping for planning and environmental studies
- GIS to CAD: survey and GIS data converted into DWG and DXF drawings for design teams
Khasra maps in GIS, ready to be overlaid with current drone maps.
## Remote GIS data processing for firms outside India
We offer remote processing to engineering, survey and GIS firms outside India: they send us their data and we return finished GIS and CAD outputs. All our projects so far have been in India. This is data processing only; we do not do field survey outside India.
- Digitisation and vectorisation of maps, plans and imagery
- Feature extraction from orthomosaics and point clouds
- Point cloud classification and terrain models
- Map production, attribute work and data clean-up to your QC rules
- Dedicated offshore seats: a team in India that works only on your projects, full time or part time, under your procedures and confidentiality terms

Q: Which software does your GIS team use?
ArcGIS, QGIS and AutoCAD, with outputs in the formats your team works in: shapefile, geodatabase, GeoPackage, KML/KMZ, GeoTIFF, DWG and DXF, in the coordinate system and projection you specify.
Q: Can you process GIS data for clients outside India?
Yes. Our in-house GIS team in Gurugram can process data remotely for engineering and GIS firms abroad; all our projects so far have been in India. This is data processing only; we do not do field survey outside India.
Q: Can we have a dedicated GIS team for confidential projects?
Yes. We can set up dedicated offshore seats in India that work only on your projects, under your procedures and confidentiality terms, full time or part time.
Q: Can you classify a point cloud that we captured ourselves?
Yes. Send us the LAS or LAZ files with the ground control and checkpoint coordinates and the class list you need. We classify the point cloud to ASPRS LAS classes such as ground, vegetation, buildings and water, build the DTM, DSM and contours from it, and check the results against your control and checkpoints.
Q: Which files do survey and engineering firms receive from a processing job?
Classified point clouds in LAS/LAZ, orthomosaics, DTM and DSM in GeoTIFF, contours and drawings in DWG, and GIS layers in SHP, in the coordinate system and height datum you specify, with the checkpoint results.
Q: What do you need to quote a GIS job?
A sample of the input data, the outputs and file formats you need, the coordinate system, accuracy or QC rules you follow, the volume of work, and the deadline.
